bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第127卷 。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Roll 127.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 127.

sentences.zh: 【宋紀九】 昭陽大荒落，一年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 9] Zhaoyang Dahuangluo; one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 9] The year Zhaoyang Dahuangluo—one year in all.

translations.literal: (End of heading.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝下之下元嘉三十年（癸巳，公元四五三年） 。

translations.literal: Lower second part of the Lower Annals of the Founding Ancestor the Literary Emperor, thirtieth year of Yuanjia (guisi, 453 CE).
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the Annals of Emperor Wen, Year 30 of Yuanjia (guisi, 453 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊寅，以南譙王義宣為司徒、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on wuyin, the Prince of Nanqiao Liu Yixuan was appointed Grand Mentor and Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wuyin, Liu Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao, was made Grand Mentor and Governor of Yang Province.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 蕭道成等帥氐、羌攻魏武都，魏高平鎮將苟莫於將突騎二千救之。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng and others led Di and Qiang forces to attack Wei's Wudu; Wei's Gaooping garrison commander Gou Moyu led two thousand crack cavalry to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng and others led Di and Qiang troops in an attack on the Northern Wei prefecture of Wudu; the Wei garrison commander at Gaooping, Gou Moyu, marched to the relief with two thousand picked horsemen.

sentences.zh: 道成等引還南鄭。

translations.literal: Daocheng and the others withdrew back to Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng and his forces then pulled back to Nanzheng.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 壬午，以征北將軍始興王濬為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Northern Campaigning General, Prince of Shixing Liu Jun, was appointed Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Liu Jun, Prince of Shixing and Northern Campaigning General, was appointed Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 帝怒未解，故濬久留京口；

translations.literal: The emperor's anger had not yet subsided, so Jun had long been kept at Jingkou;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath had not yet cooled, and so Jun had long been detained at Jingkou;

sentences.zh: 既除荊州，乃聽入朝。

translations.literal: once he was removed from Jingzhou, he was then permitted to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: only after his appointment to Jing Province was he allowed to come to court.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔江州刺史武陵王駿統諸軍討西陽蠻，軍於五洲。

translations.literal: On wuzi, an edict ordered the Governor of Jiang Province, Prince of Wuling Liu Jun, to command the various armies in punishing the Xiyang barbarians, encamping at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the emperor ordered Liu Jun, Prince of Wuling and Governor of Jiang Province, to take command of the armies against the Xiyang tribes and camp at Wuzhou.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 嚴道育之亡命也，上分遣使者搜捕甚急。

translations.literal: When Yan Daoyu became a fugitive, the emperor separately dispatched envoys to search and seize her with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Daoyu fled, the emperor sent out agents on all sides to hunt her down with the utmost urgency.

sentences.zh: 道育變服為尼，匿於東宮，又隨始興王濬至京口，。

translations.literal: Daoyu changed her dress and became a nun, hiding in the Eastern Palace; she also followed the Prince of Shixing Liu Jun to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu disguised herself as a nun and hid in the Eastern Palace; she later accompanied Prince Liu Jun of Shixing to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 或出止民張晤家。

translations.literal: At times she went out and lodged at the home of the commoner Zhang Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At times she stayed at the house of a commoner named Zhang Wu.

sentences.zh: 濬入朝，復載還東宮，欲與俱往江陵。

translations.literal: When Jun entered court, he again took her back to the Eastern Palace, intending to go with her together to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun came to court, he brought her back to the Eastern Palace again, planning to take her with him to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，上臨軒，濬入受拜。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the emperor held court at the hall; Jun entered to receive his appointment.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the emperor held audience; Jun entered to receive his commission.

sentences.zh: 是日，有告道育在張晤家者，上遣掩捕，得其二婢，雲道育隨征北還都。

translations.literal: That day someone reported that Daoyu was at Zhang Wu's house; the emperor sent men to seize her by surprise, capturing her two maidservants, who said Daoyu had returned to the capital with the Northern Campaigning General.
translations.idiomatic: That same day someone reported that Daoyu was at Zhang Wu's house. The emperor sent men to raid the place and seized two of her maidservants, who said Daoyu had returned to the capital with the Northern Campaigning General.

sentences.zh: 上謂濬與太子劭已斥遣道育，而聞其猶與往來，惆悵惋駭，乃命京口送二婢，須至檢覆，乃治劭、濬之罪。

translations.literal: The emperor thought that Jun and Crown Prince Shao had already driven Daoyu away, yet heard they still had dealings with her; sorrowful, regretful, and appalled, he ordered the two maidservants sent from Jingkou and said that only after they arrived and the matter was examined would he punish Shao and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed that Jun and Crown Prince Shao had already banished Daoyu, and learning that they were still in contact with her left him stricken with grief and alarm. He ordered the two maidservants brought from Jingkou and declared that he would punish Shao and Jun only after they arrived and the case could be investigated.

sentences.zh: 潘淑妃抱濬泣曰：「汝前祝詛事發，猶冀能刻意思愆；

translations.literal: Consort Pan Shuji embraced Jun and wept, saying, "When your earlier curse-magic affair came to light, one still hoped you could carve out your thoughts and repent;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Pan Shuji clasped Jun and wept, saying, "When your earlier sorcery scandal broke, I still hoped you would steel yourself to repent;

sentences.zh: 何意更藏嚴道育！

translations.literal: who would have thought you would again hide Yan Daoyu!
translations.idiomatic: how could you hide Yan Daoyu again!

sentences.zh: 上怒甚，我叩頭乞恩不能解，今何用生為！

translations.literal: The emperor's anger is very great; I kowtowed begging grace and could not appease it—what use is living now!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is furious beyond measure. I kowtowed and begged for mercy and could not move him—what is the point of going on living!

sentences.zh: 可送藥來，當先自取盡，不忍見汝禍敗也。

translations.literal: Send medicine; I shall first take it all myself—I cannot bear to see you meet ruin and disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Send me poison. I will take it first myself—I cannot bear to watch you destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」濬奮衣起曰：「天下事尋自當判，願小寬慮，必不上累！

translations.literal: " Jun flung his robe and rose, saying, "Affairs under Heaven will soon settle themselves of their own accord; please set your mind at ease a little—you will surely not be implicated!
translations.idiomatic: " Jun threw off his robe and stood up. "The affairs of the realm will soon sort themselves out. Please calm yourself a little—you will surely not be dragged down with me!

translations.literal: " (Close of quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of speech.)

sentences.zh: 己未，魏京兆王杜元寶坐謀反誅；

translations.literal: On jiwei, Wei's Prince of Jingzhao Du Yuanbao was executed for plotting rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Du Yuanbao, Prince of Jingzhao of Northern Wei, was executed for treason;

sentences.zh: 建寧王崇及其子濟南王麗皆為元寶所引，賜死。

translations.literal: the Prince of Jianning Chong and his son, the Prince of Jinan Li, were both implicated by Yuanbao and were granted death.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Jianning Chong and his son Li, Prince of Jinan, were both implicated through Yuanbao and were ordered to take their own lives.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 帝欲廢太子劭，賜始興王濬死，先與侍中王僧綽謀之；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to depose Crown Prince Shao and grant Prince of Shixing Liu Jun death; he first plotted this with Palace Attendant Wang Sengchuo;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor intended to depose Crown Prince Shao and put Prince Liu Jun of Shixing to death. He first discussed the matter with Palace Attendant Wang Sengchuo;

sentences.zh: 使僧綽尋漢魏以來廢太子、諸王典故，送尚書僕射徐湛之及吏部尚書江湛。

translations.literal: he had Sengchuo search out precedents from Han and Wei onward for deposing crown princes and princes, and sent them to Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Xu Chengzhi and Director of the Ministry of Personnel Jiang Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: he had Sengchuo gather precedents from Han and Wei times onward for deposing heirs apparent and princes, and forwarded them to Xu Chengzhi, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Jiang Zhan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 武陵王駿素無寵，故屢出外籓，不得留建康；

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Jun had never been favored, so he was repeatedly sent out to border fiefs and could not remain at Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun, Prince of Wuling, had never enjoyed favor and was repeatedly posted to provincial commands, never allowed to remain at Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 南平王鑠、建平王宏皆為帝所愛。

translations.literal: the Princes of Nanping Shuo and Jianping Hong were both loved by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: the Princes of Nanping and Jianping were both beloved of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 鑠妃，江湛之妹；

translations.literal: Shuo's consort was Jiang Zhan's younger sister;
translations.idiomatic: Shuo's consort was the younger sister of Jiang Zhan;

sentences.zh: 隨王誕妃，徐湛之之女也。

translations.literal: Prince of Sui Dan's consort was Xu Chengzhi's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: the consort of Liu Dan, Prince of Sui, was a daughter of Xu Chengzhi.

sentences.zh: 湛勸帝立鑠，湛之意欲立誕。

translations.literal: Jiang urged the emperor to establish Shuo; Xu's intent was to establish Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan urged the emperor to name Shuo heir; Xu Chengzhi favored Dan.

sentences.zh: 僧綽曰：「建立之事，仰由聖懷。

translations.literal: Sengchuo said, "The matter of establishment depends on the sagely breast.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo said, "The choice of heir rests entirely with Your Majesty's judgment.

sentences.zh: 臣謂唯宜速斷，不可稽緩。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that one should only act with swift decision and must not delay and drag.
translations.idiomatic: I believe you should act at once and not hesitate.

sentences.zh: 『當斷不斷，反受其亂。

translations.literal: 'When one ought to cut and does not cut, one instead receives disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: 'He who ought to strike and fails to strike will suffer disorder in return.'

sentences.zh: 』願以義割恩，略小不忍；

translations.literal: ' I pray you cut kinship by righteousness and set aside a little unwillingness to bear;
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to let duty override affection and put aside undue tenderness;

sentences.zh: 不爾，便應坦懷如初，無煩疑論。

translations.literal: otherwise, one ought to open the breast as at first and have no need for suspicious debate.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise you should open your heart to them as before and put an end to these suspicions.

sentences.zh: 事機雖密，易致宣廣，不可使難生虎表，取笑千載。

translations.literal: Though the occasion is secret, it is easy to cause it to be proclaimed and spread; one must not let difficulty arise at the tiger's watch and become a jest for a thousand ages."
translations.idiomatic: Even a closely guarded plan can leak and spread. You must not let trouble breed at your very gate and become a laughingstock for posterity."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿可謂能斷大事。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "You may be called able to decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are indeed capable of deciding great matters.

sentences.zh: 然此事至重，不可不殷勤三思。

translations.literal: Yet this affair is extremely weighty; one cannot but think thrice with earnest care.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is a matter of the gravest weight, and I cannot but consider it again and again with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 且彭城始亡。

translations.literal: Moreover, Pengcheng has only just perished.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Pengcheng has only just died.

sentences.zh: 人將謂我無復慈愛之道。

translations.literal: People will say I have no further way of loving-kindness."
translations.idiomatic: People will say I no longer know how to show a father's love."

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「臣恐千載之後，言陛下唯能裁弟，不能裁兒。

translations.literal: " Sengchuo said, "Your servant fears that after a thousand years people will say Your Majesty could only judge younger brothers and could not judge sons.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo said, "I fear that a thousand years hence posterity will say that Your Majesty could punish your brothers but not your sons.

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 江湛同侍坐，出閣，謂僧綽曰：「卿向言將不太傷切直！

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan had sat in attendance together; leaving the side chamber, he said to Sengchuo, "Your words just now were perhaps rather too cutting and blunt!
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan had been present at the audience. As they left the side chamber he said to Sengchuo, "What you said just now was rather too blunt and harsh!

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「弟亦恨君不直！

translations.literal: " Sengchuo said, "Your younger brother also resents that you are not blunt!
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo replied, "And I resent that you were not blunt enough!

translations.literal: " (Close of quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of speech.)

sentences.zh: 鑠自壽陽入朝，既至，失旨。

translations.literal: Shuo entered court from Shouyang; once he arrived, he lost the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuo came to court from Shouyang, he fell from favor as soon as he arrived.

sentences.zh: 帝欲立宏，嫌其非次，是以議久不決。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to establish Hong but disliked that he was out of proper order, and so the deliberation long went undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to name Hong heir but hesitated because he was not next in line of succession, and so the choice dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 每夜與湛之屏人語，或連日累夕。

translations.literal: Each night he spoke with Chengzhi apart from others, sometimes for successive days and many evenings.
translations.idiomatic: Night after night he spoke with Chengzhi in private, sometimes for days on end.

sentences.zh: 常使湛之自秉燭，繞壁檢行，慮有竊聽者。

translations.literal: He often had Chengzhi himself hold the candle and walk around the walls inspecting, fearing there were secret listeners.
translations.idiomatic: He often made Chengzhi carry the candle himself and walk the walls checking for eavesdroppers.

sentences.zh: 帝以其謀告潘淑妃，淑妃以告濬，濬馳報劭。

translations.literal: The emperor told his plan to Consort Pan Shuji; Shuji told Jun, and Jun galloped to report to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor confided his plan to Consort Pan Shuji, who told Jun, and Jun rode posthaste to warn Shao.

sentences.zh: 劭乃密與腹心隊主陳叔兒、齋帥張超之等謀為逆。

translations.literal: Shao then secretly with trusted retainers, company commander Chen Shuer, palace guard Zhang Chaozhi, and others plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then secretly plotted treason with his trusted followers, including company commander Chen Shuer and palace guard Zhang Chaozhi.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 初，帝以宗室強盛，慮有內難，特加東宮兵，使與羽林相若，至有實甲萬人。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the imperial clan was powerful the emperor feared internal difficulty and specially increased the Eastern Palace troops, making them comparable to the Feathered Forest guard, reaching as many as ten thousand men in actual armor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, fearing trouble within the clan, the emperor had greatly enlarged the Eastern Palace guard until it rivaled the imperial Feathered Forest troops—nearly ten thousand men under arms.

sentences.zh: 劭性黠而剛猛，帝深倚之。

translations.literal: Shao's nature was crafty and fierce; the emperor deeply relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was cunning and fierce by nature, and the emperor relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 及將作亂，每夜饗將士，或親自行酒。

translations.literal: When he was about to make rebellion, each night he feasted the officers and soldiers, sometimes personally going among them to pour wine.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared his coup, he feasted his officers every night and sometimes poured their wine himself.

sentences.zh: 王僧綽密以啟聞，會嚴道育婢將至，癸亥夜，劭詐為帝詔云：「魯秀謀反，汝可平明守闕，帥眾入。

translations.literal: Wang Sengchuo secretly reported this to the emperor; it happened that Yan Daoyu's maidservants were about to arrive. On the night of guihai, Shao forged an imperial edict saying, "Lu Xiu plots rebellion; at dawn you may guard the gate-towers and lead the masses in."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengchuo secretly informed the emperor. Just as Yan Daoyu's maidservants were due to arrive, on the night of guihai Shao forged an imperial order: "Lu Xiu is plotting rebellion. At dawn hold the palace gates and lead your men inside."

sentences.zh: 」因使張超之等集素所畜養兵士二千餘人，皆被甲；

translations.literal: " He then had Zhang Chaozhi and others assemble more than two thousand soldiers he had long kept and trained, all donning armor;
translations.idiomatic: He then had Zhang Chaozhi and others muster more than two thousand soldiers he had long kept in his household, all in armor;

sentences.zh: 召內外幢隊主副，豫加部勒，雲有所討。

translations.literal: he summoned the chief and deputy commanders of inner and outer pennant companies, preliminarily giving them orders, saying there was something to punish.
translations.idiomatic: and summoned the chief and deputy commanders of the inner and outer guard companies, telling them in advance that an operation was afoot.

sentences.zh: 夜，呼前中庶子右軍長史蕭斌、左衛率袁叔、中舍人殷仲素、左積弩將軍王正見並入宮。

translations.literal: At night he called the former Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent and Right Army Chief Clerk Xiao Bin, Left Guard Commander Yuan Shu, Palace Secretary Yin Zhongsu, and Left Strongbow General Wang Zhengjian, all to enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That night he summoned Xiao Bin, former Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent and chief clerk of the Right Army; Yuan Shu, commander of the Left Guard; Yin Zhongsu, palace secretary; and Wang Zhengjian, Left Strongbow General—all into the palace.

sentences.zh: 劭流涕謂曰：「主上信讒，將見罪廢。

translations.literal: Shao, weeping, said to them, "The sovereign believes slander and is about to punish and depose me.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, in tears, told them, "The emperor believes slanders against me and is about to depose me.

sentences.zh: 內省無過，不能受枉。

translations.literal: Inward examination finds no fault; I cannot accept wrongful treatment.
translations.idiomatic: I know myself to be innocent and cannot accept this injustice.

sentences.zh: 明旦當行大事，望相與戮力。

translations.literal: Tomorrow at dawn I shall carry out the great affair; I hope you will exert your strength together with me."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow at dawn I shall act. I ask you to join your strength to mine."

sentences.zh: 」因起，遍拜之。

translations.literal: " He then rose and bowed to them all in turn.
translations.idiomatic: He then rose and bowed to each of them in turn.

sentences.zh: 眾驚愕，莫能對。

translations.literal: The assembly was startled and dumbfounded; none could reply.
translations.idiomatic: They were stunned and speechless.

sentences.zh: 久之，淑、斌皆曰：「自古無此，願加善思！

translations.literal: After a long while, Shu and Bin both said, "From antiquity there has been nothing like this; we pray you add good reflection!
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence, Shu and Bin both said, "Nothing like this has ever been done in history. We beg you to reconsider!

sentences.zh: 」劭怒，變色。

translations.literal: " Shao grew angry and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Shao flushed with anger.

sentences.zh: 斌懼，與眾俱曰：「當竭身奉命。

translations.literal: Bin was afraid; together with the assembly he said, "We shall exhaust our persons to receive your command."
translations.idiomatic: Bin, frightened, joined the others in saying, "We will give our lives to obey."

sentences.zh: 」淑叱之曰：「卿便謂殿下真有是邪？

translations.literal: " Shu shouted at him, "Do you then suppose His Highness truly has this intent?
translations.idiomatic: Shu shouted at him, "Do you really believe His Highness means to do this?

sentences.zh: 殿下幼嘗患風，或是疾動耳。

translations.literal: His Highness in youth once suffered from wind illness; perhaps it is only the ailment stirring."
translations.idiomatic: His Highness suffered from fits in childhood—perhaps this is only his old illness returning."

sentences.zh: 」劭愈怒，因眄淑曰：「事當克不？

translations.literal: " Shao grew still angrier and, glaring at Shu, said, "Will the affair succeed or not?
translations.idiomatic: Shao grew still angrier and, glaring at Shu, demanded, "Will it succeed or not?

sentences.zh: 」淑曰：「居不疑之地，何患不克！

translations.literal: " Shu said, "Occupying a place without doubt, what worry is there of not succeeding!
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "You stand in a position beyond question—how could you fail!

sentences.zh: 但恐既克之後，不為天地所容，大禍亦旋至耳。

translations.literal: I only fear that after succeeding, one will not be borne by Heaven and Earth, and great calamity will also swiftly arrive."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear that once you succeed, Heaven and Earth will not bear you, and great disaster will follow at once."

sentences.zh: 假有此謀，猶將可息。

translations.literal: Even if there were such a plot, it could still be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you truly mean this, it is not yet too late to stop.

sentences.zh: 」左右引淑出，曰：「此何事，而雲可罷乎！

translations.literal: " Attendants led Shu out, saying, "What affair is this, that you say it can be stopped!
translations.idiomatic: Attendants dragged Shu away, crying, "What affair is this that you say can be stopped!

sentences.zh: 」淑還省，繞床行，至四更乃寢。

translations.literal: " Shu returned to his quarters, walked around his bed, and only at the fourth watch lay down to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Shu went back to his quarters, paced around his bed until the fourth watch, and only then lay down.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 甲子，宮門未開，劭以朱衣加戎服上，乘畫輪車，與蕭斌同載，衛從如常入朝之儀。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the palace gates had not yet opened; Shao placed vermilion robes over his military dress, rode a painted-wheel carriage, and shared the carriage with Xiao Bin; guards and followers were as in the usual ceremony for entering court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, before the palace gates had opened, Shao put vermilion robes over his armor, entered a painted carriage with Xiao Bin, and approached the palace with his escort in the ordinary manner of a court audience.

sentences.zh: 呼袁淑甚急，淑眠不起，劭停車奉化門催之相續。

translations.literal: He called Yuan Shu with great urgency; Shu slept and would not rise. Shao stopped the carriage at Fenghua Gate and urged him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently summoned Yuan Shu, who would not get up. Shao halted at Fenghua Gate and sent messenger after messenger to hurry him.

sentences.zh: 淑徐起，至車後；

translations.literal: Shu slowly rose and came to the rear of the carriage;
translations.idiomatic: Shu rose at last and came to the rear of the carriage;

sentences.zh: 劭使登車，又辭不上，劭命左右殺之。

translations.literal: Shao had him mount the carriage; he again declined and would not mount; Shao ordered his attendants to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao told him to get in; Shu refused again, and Shao ordered his men to kill him.

sentences.zh: 守門開，從萬春門入。

translations.literal: The gate guards opened the gates; he entered by Wanchun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeepers opened the gates, and he entered through Wanchun Gate.

sentences.zh: 舊制，東宮隊不得入城。

translations.literal: By old regulation, Eastern Palace companies might not enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: By established rule, Eastern Palace troops were not permitted inside the capital walls.

sentences.zh: 劭以偽詔示門衛曰：「受敕，有所收討。

translations.literal: Shao showed the forged edict to the gate guards, saying, "Having received an order, there is something to seize and punish."
translations.idiomatic: Shao showed the forged edict to the gate guards, saying, "By imperial command—we are to make an arrest."

sentences.zh: 」令後隊速來。

translations.literal: " He ordered the rear companies to come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the rear guard to follow at once.

sentences.zh: 張超之等數十人馳入雲龍門及齋閣，拔刀徑上合殿。

translations.literal: Zhang Chaozhi and several dozen others galloped into Yunlong Gate and the fasting chambers, drew swords, and went straight up to the Hall of Union.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chaozhi and several dozen men galloped through Yunlong Gate and the inner chambers, swords drawn, straight to the Hall of Union.

sentences.zh: 帝其夜與徐湛之屏人語至旦，燭猶未滅，門階戶席直衛兵尚寢未起。

translations.literal: That night the emperor had spoken with Xu Chengzhi apart from others until dawn; the candles were still not extinguished; the gate-steps, door, mat, and straight guards were still asleep and had not risen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had talked with Xu Chengzhi in private until dawn; the candles were still burning, and the guards at the doors and thresholds were still asleep.

sentences.zh: 帝見超之入，舉幾捍之，五指皆落，遂弒之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw Chaozhi enter, raised a table to ward him off, and all five fingers fell away; he was then assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw Chaozhi enter, he raised a table to fend him off and lost all five fingers on his hand; then they killed him.

sentences.zh: 湛之驚起，趣北戶，未及開，兵人殺之。

translations.literal: Chengzhi started up in alarm and rushed to the north door; before he could open it, the soldiers killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi sprang up in alarm and ran for the north door, but before he could open it the assassins cut him down.

sentences.zh: 劭進至合殿中閣，聞帝已殂，出坐東堂，蕭斌執刀侍直，呼中書舍人顧嘏，嘏震懼，不時出，既至，問曰：「欲共見廢，何不早啟？

translations.literal: Shao advanced to the central pavilion of the Hall of Union; hearing the emperor had already died, he went out and sat in the Eastern Hall. Xiao Bin held a sword standing in attendance. He called Palace Secretary Gu Gu; Gu was shaken with fear and did not come out promptly. Once he arrived, Shao asked, "You wished to be deposed together—why did you not report early?
translations.idiomatic: Shao advanced to the central pavilion of the Hall of Union. Learning that the emperor was dead, he went out and took his seat in the Eastern Hall while Xiao Bin stood guard with drawn sword. He summoned Palace Secretary Gu Gu, who came late, trembling with fear. When Gu arrived, Shao demanded, "If you knew we were to be deposed together, why did you not warn me sooner?

sentences.zh: 」嘏未及答，即於前斬之。

translations.literal: " Before Gu could answer, he was beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Before Gu could answer, Shao had him cut down where he stood.

sentences.zh: 江湛直上省，聞喧噪聲，歎曰：「不用王僧綽言，以至於此！

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan went straight up to the Secretariat; hearing the clamor, he sighed and said, "Not using Wang Sengchuo's words has led to this!
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan was on his way to the Secretariat when he heard the uproar. He sighed, "Because we did not heed Wang Sengchuo, it has come to this!

sentences.zh: 」乃匿傍小屋中，劭遣兵就殺之。

translations.literal: " He then hid in a small house nearby; Shao sent soldiers to go and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He hid in a cottage nearby, and Shao sent men to hunt him down and kill him.

sentences.zh: 宿衛舊將羅訓、徐罕皆望風屈附。

translations.literal: The old palace guard generals Luo Xun and Xu Han both, seeing the wind, bent and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The veteran palace guards Luo Xun and Xu Han both submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 左細仗主、廣威將軍吳興卜天與不暇被甲，執刀持弓，疾呼左右出戰。

translations.literal: The chief of the Left Fine Arms, General of Expansive Might Bu Tianyu of Wuxing, had no time to don armor; grasping knife and bow, he urgently called his attendants to go out and fight.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Tianyu of Wuxing, chief of the Left Fine Arms and General of Expansive Might, had no time to arm himself. Sword in one hand and bow in the other, he shouted for his men to sally out and fight.

sentences.zh: 徐罕曰：「殿下入，汝欲何為！

translations.literal: Xu Han said, "His Highness is entering—what do you intend!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Han cried, "His Highness is coming in—what do you think you are doing!

sentences.zh: 」天與罵曰：「殿下常來，雲何於今乃作此語！

translations.literal: " Tianyu cursed, "His Highness often comes—why do you speak such words only now!
translations.idiomatic: Tianyu cursed him: "His Highness comes here all the time—how dare you say such a thing now!

sentences.zh: 只汝是賊！

translations.literal: You alone are the traitor!
translations.idiomatic: You are the traitor!

sentences.zh: 」手射劭於東堂。

translations.literal: " He shot at Shao by hand in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed an arrow at Shao in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 幾中之。

translations.literal: He nearly hit him.
translations.idiomatic: The shot nearly struck home.

sentences.zh: 劭黨擊之，斷臂而死。

translations.literal: Shao's faction struck him; his arm was severed and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's men cut him down, severing his arm, and he died.

sentences.zh: 隊將張泓之、朱道欽、陳滿與天與俱戰死。

translations.literal: Company commanders Zhang Hongzhi, Zhu Daoqin, and Chen Man died in battle together with Tianyu.
translations.idiomatic: Company commanders Zhang Hongzhi, Zhu Daoqin, and Chen Man fell fighting beside Tianyu.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍尹弘惶怖通啟，求受處分。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Yin Hong, fearful and terrified, reported through the channels and asked to receive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Yin Hong, terrified, sent in a report asking to be punished.

sentences.zh: 劭使人從東閣入，殺潘淑妃及太祖親信左右數十人，急召始興王使帥眾屯中堂。

translations.literal: Shao sent men in through the Eastern Side Gate, killed Consort Pan Shuji and several dozen of the Founding Ancestor's trusted attendants, and urgently summoned the Prince of Shixing to lead the masses and encamp in the Central Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent men in through the Eastern Side Gate, killed Consort Pan Shuji and dozens of the late emperor's closest attendants, and urgently summoned the Prince of Shixing to bring his troops to the Central Hall.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 濬時在西州，府舍人朱法瑜告濬曰：「台內喧噪，宮門皆閉，道上傳太子反，未測禍變所至。

translations.literal: Jun was then at Xizhou; the mansion attendant Zhu Fayu told Jun, "Within the Terrace there is clamor; the palace gates are all closed; on the roads they say the crown prince has rebelled—we cannot fathom where the calamity will reach.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was at Xizhou when his mansion attendant Zhu Fayu told him, "There is uproar inside the palace compound, every gate is shut, and the streets are full of talk that the crown prince has rebelled. No one knows how far the disaster will spread.

sentences.zh: 」濬陽驚曰：「今當奈何？

translations.literal: " Jun feigned surprise and said, "What should we do now?
translations.idiomatic: Jun pretended alarm. "What are we to do now?

sentences.zh: 」法瑜勸入據石頭。

translations.literal: " Fayu urged him to enter and seize Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Fayu urged him to enter Shitou Fortress and hold it.

sentences.zh: 濬未得劭信，不知事之濟不，騷擾不知所為。

translations.literal: Jun had not yet received Shao's message and did not know whether the affair would succeed; agitated, he did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had not yet heard from Shao and did not know whether the coup had succeeded. In confusion he did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 將軍王慶曰：「今宮內有變，未知主上安危，凡在臣子，當投袂赴難；

translations.literal: General Wang Qing said, "Now there is change within the palace; we do not know whether the sovereign is safe or in peril. All who are subjects ought to fling their sleeves and rush to the difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Qing said, "There is turmoil in the palace and we do not know whether the emperor is alive. Every loyal subject should rush to his aid;

sentences.zh: 憑城自守，非臣節也。

translations.literal: to rely on a city and hold oneself—that is not the conduct of a subject."
translations.idiomatic: to shut ourselves up in a fortress is not the conduct of a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 」濬不聽，乃從南門出，逕向石頭，文武從者千餘人。

translations.literal: " Jun would not listen; he then went out by the South Gate and went straight to Shitou, with more than a thousand civil and military followers.
translations.idiomatic: Jun would not listen. He went out the South Gate straight for Shitou with more than a thousand officials and soldiers in his train.

sentences.zh: 時南平王鑠戍石頭，兵十亦千餘人。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Nanping Shuo was garrisoning Shitou, with troops also numbering more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuo of Nanping was then garrisoning Shitou with another thousand-odd troops.

sentences.zh: 俄而劭遣張超之馳馬召濬，濬屏人問狀，即戎服乘馬而去。

translations.literal: Shortly Shao sent Zhang Chaozhi galloping on horseback to summon Jun; Jun dismissed others and asked the situation, then donned military dress, mounted a horse, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shao sent Zhang Chaozhi galloping to summon Jun. Jun questioned him in private, then armed himself, mounted, and rode off.

sentences.zh: 朱法瑜固止濬，濬不從；

translations.literal: Zhu Fayu firmly tried to stop Jun, but Jun would not obey;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fayu tried hard to stop him, but Jun would not listen;

sentences.zh: 出中門，王慶又諫曰：「太子反逆，天下怨憤。

translations.literal: as he went out the central gate, Wang Qing again remonstrated, saying, "The crown prince has rebelled and turned traitor; all under Heaven resent and rage.
translations.idiomatic: as he passed the central gate Wang Qing pleaded again: "The crown prince is a traitor and the realm is furious with him.

sentences.zh: 明公但當堅閉城門，坐食積粟，不過三日，凶黨自離。

translations.literal: My lord need only firmly close the city gates, sit and eat stored grain—within no more than three days the villainous faction will scatter of itself.
translations.idiomatic: You need only shut the gates tight and live on your stores. In three days the rebels will fall apart on their own.

sentences.zh: 公情事如此，今豈宜去！

translations.literal: My lord's situation is thus—how can you now be fit to go!
translations.idiomatic: Given your position, how can you go to him now!

sentences.zh: 」濬曰：「皇太子令，敢有復言者斬！

translations.literal: " Jun said, "By the crown prince's order—whoever speaks again shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "By order of the crown prince—anyone who speaks again dies!

sentences.zh: 」既入，見劭，劭謂濬曰：「潘淑妃遂為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: " Once inside, he saw Shao; Shao said to Jun, "Consort Pan Shuji was finally harmed by the mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered and met Shao, Shao told him, "Consort Pan Shuji was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 」濬曰：「此是下情由來所願。

translations.literal: " Jun said, "This is what my lower feelings have long wished.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "That is what I have long wished for.

translations.literal: " (Close of quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of speech.)

sentences.zh: 劭詐以太祖詔召大將軍義恭、尚書令何尚之入，拘於內；

translations.literal: Shao forged an edict of the Founding Ancestor to summon Grand General Yigong and Director of the Department of State Affairs He Shangzhi to enter, and detained them within;
translations.idiomatic: Shao forged an imperial summons for Grand General Yigong and Director He Shangzhi and detained them inside the palace;

sentences.zh: 並召百官，至者才數十人。

translations.literal: he also summoned the hundred officials, but only several tens arrived.
translations.idiomatic: he also summoned the officials, but only a few dozen came.

sentences.zh: 劭遽即位；

translations.literal: Shao hastily took the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Shao immediately proclaimed himself emperor;

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「徐湛之、江湛弒逆無狀，吾勒兵入殿，已無所及，號惋崩衄，肝心破裂。

translations.literal: he issued an edict saying, "Xu Chengzhi and Jiang Zhan committed regicide without form; I led troops into the hall but could not reach them in time—I wailed and lamented, my nose burst with grief, my liver and heart split.
translations.idiomatic: and issued an edict: "Xu Chengzhi and Jiang Zhan have committed outrageous regicide. I led troops into the palace but arrived too late. My grief is unbearable and my heart is torn apart.

sentences.zh: 今罪人斯得，元兇克珍，可大赦，改元太初。

translations.literal: Now the guilty are obtained and the chief culprit is destroyed; a general amnesty may be proclaimed, and the era name changed to Taichu."
translations.idiomatic: The criminals are now caught and the chief culprit destroyed. Let there be a general amnesty and let the era name be changed to Taichu."

translations.literal: (Close of edict.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of edict.)

sentences.zh: 即位畢，亟稱疾還永福省，不敢臨喪；

translations.literal: When the enthronement was finished, he quickly claimed illness and returned to Yongfu Palace, not daring to attend the mourning;
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the ceremony was over he pleaded illness and withdrew to Yongfu Palace, not daring to attend his father's lying-in-state;

sentences.zh: 以白刃自守，夜則列燈以防左右。

translations.literal: with bare blades he guarded himself, and at night lined lamps to guard against those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: he kept drawn swords at hand and at night set lamps in rows to watch those around him.

sentences.zh: 以蕭斌為尚書僕射、領軍將軍，以何尚之為司空，前右衛率檀和之戍石頭，征虜將軍營道侯義綦鎮京口。

translations.literal: He appointed Xiao Bin Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and General Who Leads the Army; He Shangzhi as Minister of Works; the former Right Guard Commander Tan Hezhi to garrison Shitou; and the Northern Campaigning General, Marquis of Yingdao Yigi, to guard Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He made Xiao Bin Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and commanding general of the army, He Shangzhi Minister of Works, Tan Hezhi garrison commander at Shitou, and Yigi, Marquis of Yingdao and Northern Campaigning General, military governor at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 義綦，義慶之弟也。

translations.literal: Yigi was Yiqing's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yigi was the younger brother of Liu Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，悉收先給諸處兵還武庫，殺江、徐親黨尚書左丞荀赤松、右丞臧凝之等。

translations.literal: On yichou, he collected all troops previously issued to various places back to the armory, and killed Jiang and Xu's kin-party—the Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Xun Chisong, Right Assistant Director Zang Ningzhi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he recalled all troops previously issued to the provinces to the armory and executed Jiang and Xu's associates, including Left Assistant Director Xun Chisong and Right Assistant Director Zang Ningzhi.

sentences.zh: 凝之。

translations.literal: Ningzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ningzhi.

sentences.zh: 燾之孫也。

translations.literal: He was Zhaozhi's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: He was a grandson of Huan Zhaozhi.

sentences.zh: 以殷仲素為黃門侍郎，王正見為左軍將軍，張超之、陳叔兒等皆拜官、賞賜有差。

translations.literal: He appointed Yin Zhongsu Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Wang Zhengjian Left Army General; Zhang Chaozhi, Chen Shuer, and others all received offices and rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yin Zhongsu Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Wang Zhengjian Left Army General; Zhang Chaozhi, Chen Shuer, and the rest received offices and rewards according to their rank.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍魯秀在建康，劭謂秀曰：「徐湛之常欲相危，我已為卿除之矣。

translations.literal: Supporting-State General Lu Xiu was at Jiankang; Shao said to Xiu, "Xu Chengzhi often wished to endanger you—I have already removed him for you.
translations.idiomatic: Supporting-State General Lu Xiu was in Jiankang. Shao told him, "Xu Chengzhi was always plotting against you. I have already removed him for you.

sentences.zh: 」使秀與屯騎校尉龐秀之對掌軍隊。

translations.literal: " He had Xiu and the Commandant of Encamped Cavalry Pang Xiuzhi jointly command the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He paired Xiu with Commandant of Encamped Cavalry Pang Xiuzhi to share command of the army.

sentences.zh: 劭不知王僧綽之謀，以僧綽為吏部尚書，司徒左長史何偃為侍中。

translations.literal: Shao did not know Wang Sengchuo's plot; he appointed Sengchuo Director of the Ministry of Personnel and the Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat He Yan as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Unaware of Wang Sengchuo's role in the plot against him, Shao appointed Sengchuo Director of the Ministry of Personnel and He Yan, Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat, as Palace Attendant.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 武陵王駿屯五洲，沈慶之自巴水來，咨受軍略。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Jun was encamped at Wuzhou; Shen Qingzhi came from the Ba River and received consultation on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liu Jun of Wuling was camped at Wuzhou. Shen Qingzhi came up from the Ba River to receive his orders.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙亥，典簽董元嗣自建康至五洲，具言太子殺逆，駿使元嗣以告僚佐。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yihai, Registrar Dong Yuansi came from Jiankang to Wuzhou and fully related that the crown prince had killed and rebelled; Jun had Yuansi report this to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yihai, Registrar Dong Yuansi arrived at Wuzhou from Jiankang with full word that the crown prince had murdered the emperor and seized power. Jun had him inform his staff.

sentences.zh: 沈慶之密謂腹心曰：「蕭斌婦人，其餘將帥，皆易與耳。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi secretly said to his trusted men, "Xiao Bin is a woman; the rest of the generals are all easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi told his confidants in private, "Xiao Bin is no soldier, and the other commanders will be easy to handle.

sentences.zh: 東宮同惡，不過三十人；

translations.literal: Those of one mind with evil in the Eastern Palace are no more than thirty;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace conspirators number no more than thirty;

sentences.zh: 此外屈逼，必不為用。

translations.literal: beyond that, those coerced will certainly not be used.
translations.idiomatic: the rest were forced into it and will not fight for him.

sentences.zh: 今輔順討逆，不憂不濟也。

translations.literal: Now in aiding the compliant and punishing the rebel, there is no worry of not succeeding."
translations.idiomatic: If we uphold the lawful heir and punish the traitor, we cannot fail."

translations.literal: (Close of quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of speech.)

sentences.zh: 壬午，魏尊保太后為皇太后，追贈祖考，官爵兄弟，皆如外戚。

translations.literal: On renwu, Wei honored the Protecting Empress Dowager as Empress Dowager, posthumously enfeoffed her ancestors, and offices, ranks, and brothers were all as for maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Northern Wei elevated the Protecting Empress Dowager to full empress dowager, ennobled her ancestors posthumously, and granted her brothers the privileges of imperial affines.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 太子劭分浙江五郡為會州，省揚州，立司隸校尉，以其妃父殷沖為司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Shao divided the five commanderies of Zhejiang into Huizhou, reduced Yang Province, established the Director of the Retainers, and appointed his consort's father Yin Chong as Director of the Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Shao carved five Zhejiang commanderies into a new Huizhou, reduced Yang Province, created the office of Director of the Retainers, and appointed his father-in-law Yin Chong to it.

sentences.zh: 沖，融之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Chong was Rong's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chong was a great-grandson of Yin Rong.

sentences.zh: 以大將軍義恭為太保，荊州刺史南譙王義宣為太尉，始興王濬為驃騎將軍，雍州刺史臧質為丹陽尹，會稽太守隨王誕為會州刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed Grand General Yigong as Grand Tutor, the Governor of Jing Province Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan as Grand Commandant, Prince of Shixing Jun as Rapid Cavalry General, the Governor of Yong Province Zang Zhi as Governor of Danyang, and the Governor of Kuaiji Prince of Sui Dan as Governor of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He named Grand General Yigong Grand Tutor, Liu Yixuan of Nanqiao Grand Commandant, Liu Jun of Shixing Rapid Cavalry General, Zang Zhi Governor of Danyang, and Liu Dan of Sui Governor of Huizhou.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 劭料檢文帝巾箱及江湛家書疏，得王僧綽所啟饗士並前代故事，甲申，收僧綽，殺之。

translations.literal: Shao examined and checked Emperor Wen's scarf-box and Jiang Zhan's household letters, obtaining Wang Sengchuo's memorial on feasting soldiers and precedents from former ages; on jiashen he seized Sengchuo and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao searched Emperor Wen's private papers and Jiang Zhan's correspondence and found Wang Sengchuo's memorial about the crown prince feasting his troops. On jiashen he arrested Sengchuo and executed him.

sentences.zh: 僧綽弟僧虔為司徒左西屬，所親鹹勸之逃，僧虔泣曰：「吾兄奉國以忠貞，撫我以慈愛，今日之事，苦不見及耳；

translations.literal: Sengchuo's younger brother Sengqian was Western Adjunct on the Left of the Secretariat; those close to him all urged him to flee. Sengqian wept and said, "My elder brother served the state with loyalty and sincerity and nurtured me with kindness and love. In today's affair, I bitterly was not included;
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo's brother Sengqian was a Western Adjunct of the Secretariat. His friends all urged him to flee. Sengqian wept and said, "My brother served the state with loyal devotion and treated me with kindness. I bitterly regret that I was not included in his fate;

sentences.zh: 若得同歸九泉，猶羽化也。

translations.literal: if I could return together to the nine springs, it would still be transformation and ascension."
translations.idiomatic: if I could join him in death, it would be a kind of deliverance."

sentences.zh: 」劭因誣北第諸王侯，雲與僧綽謀反，殺長沙悼王瑾、瑾弟臨川哀王燁、桂陽孝侯覬、新渝懷侯玠，皆劭素所惡也。

translations.literal: " Shao then falsely accused the princes and marquises of the Northern Quarters, saying they plotted rebellion with Sengchuo, and killed the Lamented Prince of Changsha Jin, Jin's younger brother the Lamented Prince of Linchuan Ye, the Filial Marquis of Guiyang Qi, and the Cherished Marquis of Xinyu Jie—all whom Shao had long hated.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then framed the princes of the Northern Quarters, claiming they had plotted with Sengchuo, and executed the Lamented Prince of Changsha Jin, his brother Ye of Linchuan, Qi of Guiyang, and Jie of Xinyu—all men Shao had long hated.

sentences.zh: 瑾義欣之子；

translations.literal: Jin was Yixin's son;
translations.idiomatic: Jin was a son of Liu Yixin;

sentences.zh: 義華，義慶之子；

translations.literal: Yihua was Yiqing's son;
translations.idiomatic: Ye was a son of Liu Yiqing;

sentences.zh: 玠，義慶之弟子也。

translations.literal: Jie was Yiqing's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was a nephew of Liu Yiqing.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 劭密與沈慶之手書，令殺武陵王駿。

translations.literal: Shao secretly sent a handwritten letter to Shen Qingzhi ordering him to kill Prince of Wuling Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Shao secretly wrote to Shen Qingzhi ordering him to kill Prince Liu Jun of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 慶之求見王，王懼，辭以疾。

translations.literal: Qingzhi requested an audience with the prince; the prince was afraid and declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi asked for an audience; the prince, afraid, pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 慶之突入，以劭書示王，王泣求入內與母訣，慶之曰：「下官受先帝厚恩，今日之事，唯力是視；

translations.literal: Qingzhi burst in, showed Shao's letter to the prince; the prince wept and begged to enter within to take leave of his mother. Qingzhi said, "Your servant received the late emperor's thick grace; in today's affair, I look only to exerting strength;
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi forced his way in and showed the prince Shao's letter. The prince wept and begged to go in and bid his mother farewell. Qingzhi said, "I owe the late emperor a great debt. In this matter I can only do my utmost;

sentences.zh: 殿下何見疑之深！

translations.literal: why does Your Highness suspect so deeply!
translations.idiomatic: why do you doubt me so deeply!

sentences.zh: 」王起再拜曰：「家國安危，皆在將軍。

translations.literal: " The prince rose and bowed twice, saying, "The safety or peril of house and state are all in the general.
translations.idiomatic: The prince rose and bowed twice. "The fate of the realm rests entirely with you, General.

sentences.zh: 」慶之即命內外勒兵。

translations.literal: " Qingzhi immediately ordered troops marshaled inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi at once ordered the army mobilized throughout the command.

sentences.zh: 府主簿顏竣曰：「今四方未知義師之舉，劭據有天府，若首尾不相應，此危道也。

translations.literal: The mansion chief clerk Yan Jun said, "Now the four quarters do not yet know of the righteous army's rising; Shao holds the heavenly storehouse—if head and tail do not correspond, this is a perilous path.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Yan Jun said, "The provinces do not yet know we have risen. Shao holds the capital. If we move before our allies are ready, we court disaster.

sentences.zh: 宜待諸鎮協謀，然後舉事。

translations.literal: One ought to wait for the various garrisons to conspire together, and only then raise the affair.
translations.idiomatic: We should wait until the provincial commands are aligned, then act.

sentences.zh: 」慶之厲聲曰：「今舉大事，而黃頭小兒皆得參預，何得不敗！

translations.literal: " Qingzhi said in a harsh voice, "Now we raise a great affair, yet yellow-headed boys all get to participate—how can we not be defeated!
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi thundered, "We are embarking on a great enterprise, and yellow-headed boys want a say in it—how can we not fail!

sentences.zh: 宜斬以徇眾！

translations.literal: He ought to be beheaded to display to the masses!
translations.idiomatic: He ought to be beheaded as an example!

sentences.zh: 」王令竣拜謝慶之，慶之曰：「君但當知筆札事耳！

translations.literal: " The prince ordered Jun to bow and apologize to Qingzhi; Qingzhi said, "You, sir, need only understand brush-and-document affairs!
translations.idiomatic: The prince made Jun apologize. Qingzhi said, "You stick to your documents!

sentences.zh: 」於是專委慶之處分。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he exclusively entrusted disposition to Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he gave Qingzhi sole command.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，內外整辦，人以為神兵。

translations.literal: Within ten days, inside and outside were put in order; people considered it a divine army.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the army was fully ready inside and out, and men called it a host sent from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 竣，延之之子也。

translations.literal: Jun was Yanzhi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun was a son of Yan Yanzhi.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 庚寅，武陵王戒嚴誓眾。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Prince of Wuling declared martial law and swore an oath to the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Prince Liu Jun of Wuling put the army on alert and addressed the troops.

sentences.zh: 以沈慶之領府司馬；

translations.literal: He appointed Shen Qingzhi to lead the mansion as Major;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Shen Qingzhi chief of staff;

sentences.zh: 襄陽太守柳元景、隨郡太守宗愨為咨議參軍，領中兵；

translations.literal: the Governors of Xiangyang Liu Yuanjing and of Suijun Zong Que as Consulting Army Adjutants, leading the central troops;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing, Governor of Xiangyang, and Zong Que, Governor of Suijun, as consulting adjutants commanding the central army;

sentences.zh: 江夏內史朱修之行平東將軍；

translations.literal: the Interior Minister of Jiangxia Zhu Xiuzhi acting as General Who Pacifies the East;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi, Interior Minister of Jiangxia, as acting General Who Pacifies the East;

sentences.zh: 記室參軍顏設為咨議參軍，領錄事，兼總內外；

translations.literal: the Recorder Army Adjutant Yan She as Consulting Army Adjutant, leading recording affairs and jointly overseeing inside and outside;
translations.idiomatic: Yan She, recorder adjutant, as consulting adjutant in charge of records and overall administration;

sentences.zh: 以咨議參軍劉延孫為長史、尋陽太守，行留府事。

translations.literal: he appointed Consulting Army Adjutant Liu Yansun as Chief Clerk and Governor of Xunyang, acting in charge of affairs left at the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Yansun, consulting adjutant, as chief clerk and Governor of Xunyang, left in charge of headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 延孫，道產之子也。

translations.literal: Yansun was Daochan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yansun was a son of Liu Daochan.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 南譙王義宣及臧質皆不受劭命，與司州刺史魯爽同舉兵以應駿。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan and Zang Zhi both did not accept Shao's orders; together with the Governor of Si Province Lu Shuang they raised troops to respond to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yixuan of Nanqiao and Zang Zhi both rejected Shao's orders and, with Lu Shuang, Governor of Si Province, raised armies in support of Jun.

sentences.zh: 質、爽俱詣江陵見義宣，且遣使勸進於王。

translations.literal: Zhi and Shuang both went to Jiangling to see Yixuan, and also sent envoys to urge advancement upon the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Shuang both went to Jiangling to see Yixuan and sent envoys urging Jun to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，臧質子敦等在建康者聞質舉兵，皆逃亡。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Zang Zhi's sons Dun and others who were at Jiankang, hearing that Zhi had raised troops, all fled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Zang Zhi's sons who were in Jiankang, hearing that their father had risen, all fled.

sentences.zh: 劭欲相慰悅，下詔曰：「臧質，國戚勳臣，方贊翼京輦，而子弟波迸，良可怪歎。

translations.literal: Shao wished to console and please them; he issued an edict saying, "Zang Zhi is an imperial kinsman and meritorious minister, just now aiding the capital carriage, yet his sons and younger brothers scatter and flee—truly strange and lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Shao tried to reassure them with an edict: "Zang Zhi is a kinsman of the throne and a meritorious minister who is even now serving the capital. That his sons should scatter in panic is truly strange and deplorable.

sentences.zh: 可遣宣譬令還，鹹復本位。

translations.literal: One may dispatch proclamation and explanation ordering them to return; all shall resume their original posts."
translations.idiomatic: Let messengers be sent to call them back; they shall all be restored to their posts."

sentences.zh: 」劭尋錄得敦，使大將軍義恭行訓杖三十，厚給賜之。

translations.literal: " Shao soon captured Dun and had Grand General Yigong administer thirty staff strokes of discipline, then richly rewarded and bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao soon captured Dun and had Grand General Yigong administer thirty strokes of the disciplinary staff, then richly rewarded him.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 癸巳，劭葬太祖於長寧陵，謚曰景皇帝，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: On guisi, Shao buried the Founding Ancestor at Changning Mausoleum, posthumous title Emperor Jing, temple name Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Shao buried the late emperor at Changning Mausoleum with the posthumous title Emperor Jing and temple name Zhongzong.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 乙未，武陵王發西陽；

translations.literal: On the day yimi, the Prince of Wuling set out from Xiyang;
translations.idiomatic: On yimi, the Prince of Wuling marched west from Xiyang;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，至尋陽。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, he arrived at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: By dingyou he had reached Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 庚子，王命顏竣移檄四方，使共討劭。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, the Prince ordered Yan Jun to circulate a proclamation to the four quarters, causing all jointly to attack Shao.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he had Yan Jun send out a call to arms across the realm, summoning every province to join in punishing Shao.

sentences.zh: 州郡承檄，翕然響應。

translations.literal: The provinces and commanderies received the proclamation and, with unified sound, responded.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and commanderies took up the manifesto and rallied to the cause as one.

sentences.zh: 南譙王義宣遣臧質引兵詣尋陽，與駿同下，留魯爽於江陵。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, sent Zang Zhi to lead troops to Xunyang, to descend together with Jun; he left Lu Shuang at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao dispatched Zang Zhi with an army to Xunyang to march south alongside Jun, while keeping Lu Shuang at Jiangling.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 劭以兗、冀二州刺史蕭思話為徐、兗二州刺史，起張永為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Shao made Xiao Sihua, Governor of Yan and Ji, Governor of Xu and Yan, and raised Zhang Yong to be Governor of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Shao transferred Xiao Sihua from the Yan-Ji governorship to Xu and Yan, and appointed Zhang Yong Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 思話自歷城引部曲還平城，起兵以應尋陽；

translations.literal: Sihua led his household troops from Licheng back to Pingcheng and raised forces to respond to Xunyang;
translations.idiomatic: Sihua withdrew his personal following from Licheng to Pingcheng and took up arms in support of the Xunyang coalition;

sentences.zh: 建武將軍垣護之在歷城，亦帥所領赴之。

translations.literal: The Jianwu General Yuan Huzhi, who was at Licheng, also led those under his command to go to them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huzhi, General of Jianwu, was also at Licheng and marched his command thither to join them.

sentences.zh: 南譙王義宣版張永為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, issued a commission appointing Zhang Yong Governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao formally commissioned Zhang Yong as Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 永遣司馬崔勳之等將兵赴義宣。

translations.literal: Yong sent his Chief Clerk Cui Xunzhi and others to lead troops to go to Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong dispatched Chief Clerk Cui Xunzhi and others with troops to join Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 義宣慮蕭思話與永不釋前憾，自為書與思話，使長史張暢為書與永，勸使相與坦懷。

translations.literal: Yixuan feared that Xiao Sihua and Yong had not released their former resentments; he himself wrote a letter to Sihua and had Chief Clerk Zhang Chang write a letter to Yong, urging them to open their hearts to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Sihua and Zhang Yong still nursed old grudges, Yixuan wrote to Sihua in his own hand and had Chief Clerk Zhang Chang write to Yong, urging both men to set aside past grievances.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 隨王誕將受劭命，參軍事沈正說司馬顧琛曰：「國家此禍，開闢未聞。

translations.literal: The Prince of Sui, Dan, was about to accept Shao's commission; the staff officer Shen Zheng persuaded the Chief Clerk Gu Chen, saying, "This calamity to the state—since the opening of the world, none has heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Sui was on the verge of accepting orders from Shao when staff officer Shen Zheng urged Chief Clerk Gu Chen: "The realm faces a disaster without precedent in all history.

sentences.zh: 今以江東驍銳之眾，唱大義於天下，其誰不響應！

translations.literal: Now, with the fierce and sharp masses of Jiangdong, proclaiming the great cause under Heaven—who would not respond in echo!
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangdong's battle-hardened armies now raising the banner of righteousness throughout the empire, who would fail to answer the call!

sentences.zh: 豈可使殿下北面凶逆，受其偽寵乎！

translations.literal: How can we allow the Prince to face north toward the violent rebel and receive his false favor!
translations.idiomatic: How can we let His Highness bow to a regicide and accept honors from a usurper!

sentences.zh: 」琛曰：「江東忘戰日久，雖逆順不同，然強弱亦異，當須四方有義舉者，然後應之，不為晚也。

translations.literal: Chen said: "Jiangdong has forgotten warfare for a long time; though rebel and loyal differ, yet strong and weak also differ—one must wait until the four quarters have righteous uprisings, and then respond; it would not be late.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen replied: "Jiangdong has grown unused to war. Right may differ from wrong, but our strength does not match theirs—we should wait until righteous forces rise elsewhere, then join them; that would not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」正曰：「天下未嘗有無父無君之國，寧可自安仇恥而責義於餘方乎！

translations.literal: Zheng said: "Under Heaven there has never been a state without father and without sovereign—how can one seek ease amid shame and enmity while charging others with righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zheng answered: "No kingdom has ever endured without filial duty or loyalty to its ruler. How can we hide in comfort while our honor lies in ruins and demand that others bear the burden of righteousness!

sentences.zh: 今正以弒逆冤丑，義不同天，舉兵之日，豈求必全邪！

translations.literal: Now we take as our cause the parricide and rebel, whose righteousness is opposed as heaven to earth—on the day we raise arms, how could we seek certain preservation!
translations.idiomatic: We march against a son who murdered his father—a crime that puts us at irreconcilable odds with Heaven itself. When we take up arms, can we expect to come through unscathed?

sentences.zh: 馮衍有言：『大漢之貴臣，將不如荊、齊之賤士乎！

translations.literal: Feng Yan once had a saying: 'The honored minister of Great Han—would he not be as the lowly scholar of Jing and Qi!
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yan once wrote: 'Shall a great minister of Han rank lower than the humblest men of Jing and Qi!

sentences.zh: 』況殿下義兼臣子，事實國家者哉！

translations.literal: ' Moreover, the Prince's righteousness embraces both subject and son—how much more one who in fact serves the state!
translations.idiomatic: 'And Your Highness owes duty both as a subject and as a son—how much more so to the realm itself!

sentences.zh: 」琛乃與正共入說誕，誕從之。

translations.literal: Chen then together with Zheng entered to persuade Dan, and Dan followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen and Shen Zheng then went in together to persuade Prince Dan, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 正，田子之兄子也。

translations.literal: Zheng was the son of Tianzi's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zheng was a nephew of Tianzi.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 劭自謂素習武事，語朝士曰：「卿等但助我理文書，勿措意戎旅；

translations.literal: Shao considered himself long practiced in military affairs and said to the court officials: "You need only assist me in handling documents—do not set your minds on military campaigns;
translations.idiomatic: Shao, confident in his martial experience, told the court: "Leave the paperwork to me—do not trouble yourselves with the conduct of war;

sentences.zh: 若有寇難，吾自當之，但恐賊虜不敢動耳。

translations.literal: if there is bandit difficulty, I myself will take it on—I only fear the rebel bandits dare not move.
translations.idiomatic: should enemies appear, I will meet them myself. I only worry the rebels may not dare stir at all.

sentences.zh: 」及聞四方兵起，始憂懼，戒嚴，悉召下番將吏，遷淮南岸居民於北岸，盡聚諸王及大臣於城內，移江夏王義恭處尚書下捨，分義恭諸子處侍中下省。

translations.literal: When he heard that troops had risen in the four quarters, he then began to worry and fear; he declared martial law, summoned all off-duty generals and officials, moved residents of the south Huai bank to the north bank, gathered all princes and great ministers within the city, moved the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, to lodge below the Secretariat, and distributed Yigong's sons to the attendants' lower quarters.
translations.idiomatic: But when word came that armies were rising everywhere, fear took hold. He imposed martial law, recalled every off-duty officer, evacuated the south bank of the Huai, concentrated princes and senior ministers inside the capital, quartered Prince Yigong of Jiangxia beneath the Secretariat offices, and dispersed Yigong's sons to the attendants' lower chambers.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸卯朔，柳元景統寧朔將軍薛安都等十二軍發湓口，司空中兵參軍徐遺寶以荊州之眾繼之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day of the cycle guimao: Liu Yuanyin commanded twelve armies including the Ningsuo General Xue Andu and others, setting out from Penkou; the Grand Master of Works and Central Army Aide Xu Yibao followed with the masses of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day guimao, Liu Yuanjing led twelve armies—including General of Ningsuo Xue Andu—from Penkou, while Grand Master of Works Xu Yibao, serving as central-army aide, followed with the Jingzhou forces.

sentences.zh: 丁未，武陵王發尋陽，沈慶之總中軍以從。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, the Prince of Wuling set out from Xunyang; Shen Qingzhi commanded the central army and followed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the Prince of Wuling marched out of Xunyang, with Shen Qingzhi in command of the central army.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 劭立妃殷氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Shao established Consort Yin as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Shao installed Lady Yin as empress.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 庚戌，武陵王檄書至建康，劭以示太常顏延之曰：「彼誰筆也？

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, the Prince of Wuling's proclamation arrived at Jiankang; Shao showed it to the Grand Commandant of Ceremonies Yan Yanzhi and said, "Whose brush is that?
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Prince of Wuling's manifesto reached Jiankang. Shao showed it to Yan Yanzhi, Grand Commandant of Ceremonies, and asked: "Who wrote this?

sentences.zh: 」延之曰：「竣之筆也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi said: "It is Jun's brush.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi replied: "Yan Jun's hand."

sentences.zh: 」劭曰：「言辭何至於是！

translations.literal: Shao said: "How could the words reach to such a point!
translations.idiomatic: Shao exclaimed: "How could the language go so far!

sentences.zh: 」延之曰：「竣尚不顧老臣，安能顧陛下！

translations.literal: Yanzhi said: "Jun does not even regard an old minister—how could he regard Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi answered: "If Jun spares no thought for an old servant of the court, why would he spare any for Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 」劭怒稍解。

translations.literal: Shao's anger gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's rage slowly eased.

sentences.zh: 悉拘武陵王子於侍中下省，南譙王義宣子於太倉空捨。

translations.literal: He detained all the sons of the Prince of Wuling at the attendants' lower quarters, and the sons of the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, in the empty storehouses of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Prince of Wuling's sons in the attendants' lower chambers and Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao's sons in vacant Taicang warehouses as hostages.

sentences.zh: 劭欲盡殺三鎮士民家口，江夏王義恭、何尚之皆曰：「凡舉大事者不顧家；

translations.literal: Shao wished to kill to the last all the families of the soldiers and common people of the three garrisons; the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, and He Shangzhi both said, "All who undertake great affairs do not consider their households;
translations.idiomatic: Shao wanted to exterminate the families of every man from the three frontier garrisons. Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and He Shangzhi both argued: "Men who join a great cause do not let family ties hold them back;

sentences.zh: 且多是驅逼，今忽誅其室累，正足堅彼意耳。

translations.literal: moreover, most were driven and compelled—if we now suddenly execute their wives and dependents, that would only harden their resolve.
translations.idiomatic: and most of them were pressed into service against their will. Slaughter their kin now, and you will only steel their determination.

sentences.zh: 」劭以為然，乃下書一無所問。

translations.literal: Shao thought this correct and then issued an edict holding no one accountable for anything.
translations.idiomatic: Shao accepted the advice and issued an order declaring a general amnesty.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 劭疑朝廷舊臣皆不為己用，乃厚撫魯秀及右軍參軍王羅漢，悉以軍事委之；

translations.literal: Shao suspected that the old ministers of the court would none serve him; he therefore treated Lu Xiu and the Right Army Aide Wang Luohan generously and entrusted all military affairs to them;
translations.idiomatic: Distrusting the veteran court officials, Shao lavished favors on Lu Xiu and Right Army aide Wang Luohan and placed the whole military command in their hands;

sentences.zh: 以蕭斌為謀主，殷沖掌文符。

translations.literal: he made Xiao Bin chief strategist, and Yin Chong managed documents and seals.
translations.idiomatic: he named Xiao Bin his chief adviser and put Yin Chong in charge of dispatches and seals.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌勸劭勒水軍自上決戰，不爾則保據梁山。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin urged Shao to lead the navy upstream for a decisive battle; if not, then hold and defend Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin counseled Shao to take the fleet upriver and force a decisive engagement—or, failing that, to fortify Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭以南軍倉猝，船舫陋小，不利水戰，乃進策曰：「賊駿小年未習軍旅，遠來疲弊，宜以逸待之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, because the southern army was hasty and its boats and ships crude and small, unfavorable for water combat, then advanced a plan, saying, "The rebel Jun is young and has not practiced military campaigns; coming from afar, he is weary and exhausted—one should await him with rested forces.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, noting that the southern forces had been raised in haste and their vessels were small and unfit for river fighting, proposed instead: "The rebel Jun is young and untested in war, and his army is worn out from the long march—we should meet him with fresh troops and let fatigue do its work.

sentences.zh: 今遠出梁山，則京都空弱，東軍乘虛，或能為患。

translations.literal: If we go far out to Liangshan, then the capital will be empty and weak, and the eastern army may exploit the void and become a trouble.
translations.idiomatic: If we advance as far as Liangshan, the capital will lie exposed, and the eastern army may strike at our weakness.

sentences.zh: 若分力兩赴，則兵散勢離。

translations.literal: If we divide strength and go to both places, then the army scatters and momentum separates.
translations.idiomatic: Split our forces between two objectives, and we scatter our strength and lose cohesion.

sentences.zh: 不如養銳待期，坐而觀釁。

translations.literal: It is better to nurture sharpness and await the appointed time, sitting and watching for openings.
translations.idiomatic: Better to keep our edge, bide our time, and wait for the enemy to show a flaw.

sentences.zh: 割棄南岸，柵斷石頭，此先朝舊法，不憂賊不破也。

translations.literal: Abandon the south bank, palisade and block Shitou—this is the former court's old method; do not worry that the rebels will not be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Give up the south bank, fortify Shitou behind palisades—this was the proven strategy of earlier reigns, and the rebels cannot fail to be crushed.

sentences.zh: 」劭善之。

translations.literal: Shao approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Shao agreed.

sentences.zh: 斌厲色曰：「南中郎二十年少，能建如此大事，豈復可量！

translations.literal: Bin said with stern countenance: "The Middle Commander of the South is only twenty years old, yet he has accomplished such a great affair—how can he again be measured!
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin said sharply: "The southern heir is barely twenty, yet he has already pulled off a coup of this magnitude—who can guess what he is capable of!

sentences.zh: 三方同惡，勢據上流；

translations.literal: The three quarters share the same evil, and their momentum holds the upper stream;
translations.idiomatic: Three regions have joined against us, and they control the river above;

sentences.zh: 沈慶之甚練軍事，柳元景、宗愨屢嘗立功。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi is very practiced in military affairs; Liu Yuanyin and Zong Que have repeatedly tasted achievement in merit.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi is a seasoned commander, and Liu Yuanjing and Zong Que are proven victors.

sentences.zh: 形勢如此，實非小敵。

translations.literal: The situation being like this, they are truly not a small enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Given such odds, this is no minor foe.

sentences.zh: 唯宜及人情未離，尚可決力一戰；

translations.literal: One should only, while the people's hearts have not yet departed, still be able to decide with full force in one battle;
translations.idiomatic: We must strike now, while loyalty still holds, and stake everything on a single battle;

sentences.zh: 端坐台城，何由得久！

translations.literal: sitting upright in Taicheng—by what means can one obtain long endurance!
translations.idiomatic: sit idle behind Taicheng's walls, and how long can we last!

sentences.zh: 今主，鹹無戰意，豈非天也！

translations.literal: Now the sovereign is entirely without war intent—is this not Heaven's decree!
translations.idiomatic: Yet our ruler has no stomach for fighting at all—is this not Heaven itself turning against us!

sentences.zh: 」邵不聽。

translations.literal: (Close of quotation.) Shao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: (End of speech.) Shao would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 或勸劭保石頭城，劭曰：「昔人所以固石頭城者，俟諸侯勤王耳。

translations.literal: Some urged Shao to hold Shitou fortress; Shao said: "The reason people of old fortified Shitou fortress was to await the feudal lords coming to aid the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Others advised Shao to defend Shitou, but he replied: "Our forebears held Shitou only because they expected loyal lords to ride to the emperor's rescue.

sentences.zh: 我若守此，誰當見救！

translations.literal: If I hold here, who will come to save me!
translations.idiomatic: If I barricade myself here, who will come to my aid!

sentences.zh: 唯應力戰決之；

translations.literal: One should only exert force in battle and decide it;
translations.idiomatic: We must fight with everything we have and settle this on the field;

sentences.zh: 不然，不克。

translations.literal: if not, one cannot overcome.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise we cannot win.

sentences.zh: 」日日自出行軍，慰勞將士，親督都水治船艦。

translations.literal: Day after day he personally went out on military rounds, comforted and encouraged the soldiers, and personally supervised the Capital Water Office in repairing boats and ships.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he inspected the camps in person, rallied the troops, and oversaw the imperial shipyards as they refitted the fleet.

sentences.zh: 壬子，焚淮南岸室屋、淮內船舫，悉驅民家渡水北。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, he burned the houses on the south Huai bank and the boats and ships within the Huai, and drove all civilian households across the water to the north.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he torched every building on the south bank of the Huai and every vessel on the river, forcing all civilians to flee to the north shore.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 立子偉之為皇太子。

translations.literal: He established his son Weizhi as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Weizhi crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以始興王濬妃父褚湛之為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He appointed the father of Consort of the Prince of Shixing, Jun—Chu Zhanzhi—as Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He made Chu Zhanzhi, father of Prince Jun of Shixing's consort, Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 湛之，裕之之兄子也。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was the son of Yuzhi's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Zhanzhi was a nephew of Chu Yuzhi.

sentences.zh: 濬為侍中、中書監、司徒、錄尚書六條事，加南平王鑠開府儀同三司，以南兗州刺史建平王宏為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Jun was Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, Minister over the Masses, and Recorder of the Six Articles of the Secretariat; he added the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, as Grand General with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and made the Prince of Jianping, Hong, Governor of Jiang from Governor of South Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jun received the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Secretariat Director, Minister over the Masses, and overseer of the Six Departments; Shuo, Prince of Nanping, was granted the Grand General's seal with honors equal to the Three Excellencies; and Hong, Prince of Jianping, was transferred from South Yanzhou to govern Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 太尉司馬寵秀之自石頭先眾南奔，人情由是大震。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant's Chief Clerk, Long Xiuzhi, from Shitou went ahead of the masses and fled south; popular sentiment thereby greatly shook.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Long Xiuzhi of the Grand Commandant fled south from Shitou ahead of the crowd, and public morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 以營道侯義綦為湘州刺史，檀和之為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed the Marquis of Yingdao, Yiji, Governor of Xiang, and Tan Hezhi Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He named Marquis Yiji of Yingdao Governor of Xiangzhou and Tan Hezhi Governor of Yongzhou.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 癸丑，武陵王軍於鵲頭。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, the Prince of Wuling encamped at Quetou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the Prince of Wuling made camp at Quetou.

sentences.zh: 宣城太守王僧達得武陵王檄，未知所從。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Xuancheng, Wang Sengda, received the Prince of Wuling's proclamation and did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda, Administrator of Xuancheng, received the Prince of Wuling's manifesto and could not decide which side to take.

sentences.zh: 客說之曰：「方今釁逆滔天，古今未有。

translations.literal: A guest persuaded him, saying, "At present the rebel evil floods heaven—never in past and present.
translations.idiomatic: A visitor advised him: "The usurper's crime towers to the heavens—nothing like it has ever been seen.

sentences.zh: 為君計，莫若承義師之檄，移告傍郡。

translations.literal: For your plan as lord, nothing is better than accepting the righteous army's proclamation and sending notice to neighboring commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: My counsel, my lord: accept the manifesto of the loyal armies and spread word to the neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 苟在有心，誰不響應！

translations.literal: If they have intent in their hearts, who would not respond!
translations.idiomatic: Where men still have conscience, who would not rally!

sentences.zh: 此上策也。

translations.literal: This is the upper stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: That is the best course.

sentences.zh: 如其不能，可躬帥向義之徒，詳擇水陸之便，致身南歸，亦其次也。

translations.literal: If one cannot do that, one may personally lead those who turn toward righteousness, carefully choose the convenience of water and land routes, and dedicate oneself to returning south—this too is next.
translations.idiomatic: If that proves impossible, gather every man willing to join the righteous cause, pick the safest route by land or water, and make your way south—that is the next-best choice.

sentences.zh: 」僧達乃自侯道南奔，逢武陵王於鵲頭。

translations.literal: Sengda then, by himself from Hou Road, fled south; he met the Prince of Wuling at Quetou.
