translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda fled south by the Hou Road and joined the Prince of Wuling at Quetou.

sentences.zh: 王即以為長史。

translations.literal: The Prince immediately made him Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The prince at once appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 僧達，弘之子也。

translations.literal: Sengda was Hong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda was the son of Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 王初發尋陽，沈慶之謂人曰：「王僧達必來赴義。

translations.literal: When the Prince first set out from Xunyang, Shen Qingzhi said to people: "Wang Sengda will surely come to join the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: As the prince was leaving Xunyang, Shen Qingzhi told others: "Wang Sengda will certainly come to our side.

sentences.zh: 」人問其故，慶之曰：「吾見其在先帝前議論開張，執意明決；

translations.literal: People asked the reason; Qingzhi said: "I saw him before the Former Emperor, his discourse open and expansive, his intent bright and decisive;
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, Qingzhi said: "I once watched him debate before the late emperor—bold in speech, clear and resolute in judgment;

sentences.zh: 以此言之，其至必也。

translations.literal: speaking from this, his coming is certain.
translations.idiomatic: judging by that, his arrival is assured.

translations.literal: (Close of quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of speech.)

sentences.zh: 柳元景以舟艦不堅，憚於水戰，乃倍道兼行，丙辰，至江寧步上，使薛安帥鐵騎曜兵於淮上，移書朝士，為陳逆順。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanyin, because the boats and ships were not sturdy, feared water combat; he therefore marched at double speed, and on the day bingchen reached Jiangning on foot. He had Xue Andu lead iron cavalry to display troops on the Huai and sent letters to the court officials, setting forth rebel and loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his vessels too flimsy for river fighting, Liu Yuanjing pressed forward by forced marches; on bingchen he entered Jiangning overland, sent Xue Andu at the head of armored horsemen to show force along the Huai, and wrote to court officials laying out the case for loyalty against rebellion.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 劭加吳興太守汝南周嶠冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Shao added the Administrator of Wuxing, Zhou Qiao of Runan, as General Champion.
translations.idiomatic: Shao promoted Zhou Qiao of Runan, Administrator of Wuxing, to General Champion.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕檄亦至，嶠素恇怯，回惑不知所從；

translations.literal: The Prince of Sui, Dan's proclamation also arrived; Qiao had always been timid and fearful, and, turning and confused, did not know whom to follow;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Sui's manifesto arrived as well. Zhou Qiao, a man of habitual cowardice, wavered helplessly, unable to choose a side;

sentences.zh: 府司馬丘珍孫殺之，舉郡應誕。

translations.literal: the prefecture's Chief Clerk, Qiu Zhensun, killed him and raised the commandery to respond to Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Qiu Zhensun killed him and raised the entire commandery for Prince Dan.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 戊午，武陵王至南洲，降者相屬；

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, the Prince of Wuling reached Nanzhou; those who surrendered followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the Prince of Wuling arrived at Nanzhou, and defectors streamed in without pause.

sentences.zh: 乙未，軍於溧洲。

translations.literal: On the day yimi, the army encamped at Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yimi the army halted at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 王自發尋陽，有疾，不能見將佐，唯顏竣出入臥內，擁王於膝，親視起居。

translations.literal: From the time the Prince himself set out from Xunyang, he had an illness and could not see generals and aides; only Yan Jun entered and exited the inner chamber, embracing the Prince upon his knees and personally viewing his daily rise and rest.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he left Xunyang the prince had been ill and could not receive his officers; only Yan Jun attended him in the sickroom, holding him on his lap and watching over his every need.

sentences.zh: 疾屢危篤，不任咨稟，竣皆專決。

translations.literal: The illness repeatedly reached critical severity; unable to bear consultation and reports, Jun decided all matters exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's condition repeatedly turned grave, and when he could no longer hear petitions, Yan Jun made every decision on his own.

sentences.zh: 軍政之外，間以文教書檄，應接遐邇，昏曉臨哭，若出一人。

translations.literal: Beyond military and governmental affairs, he intermittently with civil and educational writings and proclamations responded to near and far; at dusk and dawn he attended mourning rites—as if from a single person.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from running the army and the administration, he drafted dispatches and proclamations, answered appeals from every quarter, and even led the mourning observances morning and night—as though one man alone carried the whole enterprise.

sentences.zh: 如是累旬，自舟中甲士亦不知王之危疾也。

translations.literal: Thus for successive ten-day periods, even the armored men in the boats did not know the prince's critical illness.
translations.idiomatic: Weeks passed in this way, until even the armored soldiers aboard the fleet knew nothing of the prince's grave condition.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 癸亥，柳元景潛至新亭，依山為壘。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Liu Yuanjing secretly reached Xinting and, relying on the hills, built fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Liu Yuanjing stole into Xinting and entrenched his men on the hillside.

sentences.zh: 新降者皆勸元景速進，元景曰：「不然。

translations.literal: All who had newly surrendered urged Yuanjing to advance quickly; Yuanjing said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Every recent defector pressed Yuanjing to push forward at once; Yuanjing replied, "No.

sentences.zh: 理順難恃，同惡相濟，輕進無防，實啟寇心。

translations.literal: Right principle is hard to rely on; those who share the same evil assist one another; a light advance without defense truly opens the enemy's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness alone is no guarantee; villains will rally to one another; rush in without guard and you only embolden the foe.

translations.literal: (Close of quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of speech.)

sentences.zh: 元景營未立，劭龍驤將軍詹叔兒覘知之，勸劭出戰，劭不許。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's camp was not yet established when Shao's Dragon-Steed General Zhan Shu'er reconnoitered and learned of it; he urged Shao to go out and fight, but Shao would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yuanjing's camp was fully set, Shao's Dragon-Steed General Zhan Shu'er spotted it and urged an attack; Shao refused.

sentences.zh: 甲子，劭使蕭斌統步軍，褚湛之統水軍，與魯秀、王羅漢、劉簡之等精兵合萬人，攻新亭壘，劭自登朱雀門督戰。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Shao had Xiao Bin command the infantry and Chu Zhanzhi command the navy; together with Lu Xiu, Wang Luohan, Liu Jianzhi, and other picked troops they totaled ten thousand men and attacked the Xinting fortifications, while Shao himself ascended the Vermilion Bird Gate to oversee the battle.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Shao sent Xiao Bin at the head of the foot soldiers and Chu Zhanzhi at the head of the fleet; with Lu Xiu, Wang Luohan, Liu Jianzhi, and other elite troops they mustered ten thousand men and assaulted the Xinting lines, while Shao himself took command from the Vermilion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 元景宿令軍中曰：「鼓繁氣易衰，叫數力易竭；

translations.literal: Yuanjing had ordered the army overnight, saying, "When drums are frequent, spirit easily declines; when shouting is frequent, strength easily exhausts;
translations.idiomatic: The night before, Yuanjing had told his troops, "Too much drumming drains the will; too much shouting wears out the strength;

sentences.zh: 但銜枚疾戰，一聽吾鼓聲。

translations.literal: only hold mouth-gags and fight swiftly—listen solely to my drum.
translations.idiomatic: fight in silence with bits between your teeth, and wait for my drum alone.

sentences.zh: 」劭將士懷劭重賞，皆殊死戰。

translations.literal: " Shao's officers and soldiers, cherishing Shao's heavy rewards, all fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's men, tempted by his lavish bounties, fought as though death meant nothing.

sentences.zh: 元景水陸受敵，意氣彌強，麾下勇士，悉遣出鬥，左右唯留數人宣傳。

translations.literal: Yuanjing was attacked on land and water, yet his spirit grew ever stronger; the brave warriors under his command he sent out entirely to fight, keeping only a few attendants at his side to relay orders.
translations.idiomatic: Beset on land and river alike, Yuanjing's resolve only hardened; he threw every able fighter into the fray and kept beside him only a handful of men to carry his orders.

sentences.zh: 劭兵勢垂克，魯秀擊退鼓，劭眾遽止。

translations.literal: Shao's army's momentum nearly achieved victory, but Lu Xiu beat the retreat drum and Shao's masses suddenly halted.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's force was on the verge of breaking through when Lu Xiu sounded the retreat, and the whole army stopped short.

sentences.zh: 元景乃開壘鼓噪以乘之，劭眾大潰，墜淮死者甚多。

translations.literal: Yuanjing then opened the fortifications, drummed and shouted to take advantage of them; Shao's masses greatly collapsed, and many who fell into the Huai died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing threw open the camp, raised a thunder of drums and war cries, and pressed the advantage; Shao's army broke in rout, and great numbers drowned in the Huai.

sentences.zh: 劭更帥餘眾，自來攻壘，元景復大破之，所殺傷過於前戰，士卒爭赴死馬澗，澗為之溢；

translations.literal: Shao again led the remaining masses and came in person to attack the fortifications; Yuanjing again greatly defeated them, and the killed and wounded exceeded the previous battle; soldiers raced one another into Dead Horse Stream until the stream overflowed;
translations.idiomatic: Shao rallied his survivors and led them personally against the fort again; Yuanjing routed them once more, with casualties surpassing the first fight; men trampled one another into Dead Horse Stream until the water ran over its banks;

sentences.zh: 劭手斬退者，不能禁。

translations.literal: Shao personally beheaded those retreating, yet could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao himself cut down fleeing soldiers, but nothing could halt the panic.

sentences.zh: 劉簡之死，蕭斌被創，劭僅以身免，走還宮。

translations.literal: Liu Jianzhi died; Xiao Bin was wounded; Shao barely escaped with his life and fled back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianzhi was killed, Xiao Bin was wounded, and Shao barely escaped with his life and fled back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 魯秀、褚湛之、檀和之皆南奔。

translations.literal: Lu Xiu, Chu Zhanzhi, and Tan Hezhi all fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu, Chu Zhanzhi, and Tan Hezhi all fled south.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 丙寅，武陵王至江寧。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, the Prince of Wuling reached Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the Prince of Wuling arrived at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，江夏王義恭單騎南奔；

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, fled south alone on horseback;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong, fled south alone on horseback;

sentences.zh: 劭殺義恭十二子。

translations.literal: Shao killed Yigong's twelve sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shao executed Yigong's twelve sons.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 劭、濬憂迫無計，以輦迎蔣侯神像置宮中，稽顙乞恩，拜為大司馬，封鐘山王；

translations.literal: Shao and Jun, anxious and with no plan, used an imperial carriage to welcome the divine image of Lord Jiang and placed it in the palace; they knocked their foreheads begging grace, enfeoffed it as Grand Marshal, and sealed it as Prince of Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: Desperate and out of options, Shao and Liu Jun had Lord Jiang's idol borne into the palace by imperial carriage; they kowtowed and begged for divine favor, appointing the image Grand Marshal and creating it Prince of Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 拜蘇侯神為驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: they enfeoffed the god Lord Su as General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: they also enfeoffed the god Lord Su as General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以濬為南徐州刺史，與南平王鑠並錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Jun was made Inspector of South Xuzhou and, together with the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, jointly handled the six departments of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun was made inspector of South Xuzhou and, with the Prince of Nanping, Liu Shuo, was put in joint charge of Secretariat affairs.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 戊辰，武陵王軍於新亭，大將軍義恭上表勸進。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the Prince of Wuling encamped at Xinting; the Grand General Yigong submitted a memorial urging him to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the Prince of Wuling encamped at Xinting, and Grand General Liu Yigong memorialized urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎徐愛在殿中誑劭，雲自追義恭，遂歸武陵王。

translations.literal: Gentleman Attendant at Large Xu Yuan, in the hall, deceived Shao, saying he was himself pursuing Yigong, and then returned to the Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Attendant at Large Xu Yuan, still inside the palace, deceived Shao by claiming he was riding out after Yigong, then slipped away and joined the Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 時王軍府草創，不曉朝章；

translations.literal: At that time the prince's military headquarters was newly established and did not understand court regulations;
translations.idiomatic: The prince's headquarters had only just been formed and knew nothing of court protocol;

sentences.zh: 爰素所諳練。

translations.literal: Yuan had always been versed and practiced in them.
translations.idiomatic: but Xu Yuan knew those rites inside out.

sentences.zh: 乃以爰兼太常丞，撰即位儀注。

translations.literal: He was therefore made Acting Director of the Grand Ceremonial and drafted the protocols for the accession.
translations.idiomatic: The prince therefore made him acting director of the Grand Ceremonial and charged him with drafting the accession rites.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，王即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, the prince assumed the emperor's position and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the prince took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 文武賜爵一等，從軍者二等。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were granted one rank of nobility; those who had followed the army received two.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were raised one rank in nobility; men who had marched with the army received two.

sentences.zh: 改謚大行皇帝曰文，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: The posthumous title of the late emperor was changed to Wen, and his temple name was set as Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's posthumous title was changed to Wen and his temple name to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 以大將軍義恭為太尉、錄尚書六條事、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Grand General Yigong was made Grand Commandant, put in charge of the six departments of the Secretariat, and made Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Liu Yigong was made grand commandant, given charge of Secretariat affairs, and appointed inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，劭亦臨軒拜太子偉之，大赦，唯劉駿、義恭、義宣、誕不在原例。

translations.literal: That same day, Shao also held audience from the front hall to invest the crown prince, Weizhi, and proclaimed a general amnesty, but Liu Jun, Yigong, Yixuan, and Dan alone were excluded from pardon.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Shao held court to invest his son Weizhi as crown prince and issued his own amnesty, explicitly excluding Liu Jun, Yigong, Yixuan, and Dan.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以南譙王義宣為中書監、丞相、錄尚書六條事、揚州刺史，隨王誕為衛將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史，藏質為東騎將軍，開府儀同三司、江州刺史，沈慶之為領軍將軍，蕭思話為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, was made Supervisor of the Secretariat, Chancellor, put in charge of the six departments of the Secretariat, and Inspector of Yangzhou; the Prince of Sui, Dan, was made Guard General, given the Grand Prefectural Establishment with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and made Inspector of Jingzhou; Zang Zhi was made General of the Eastern Household, given the Grand Prefectural Establishment with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and made Inspector of Jiangzhou; Shen Qingzhi was made General Who Leads the Army; and Xiao Sihua was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the Prince of Nanqiao, Liu Yixuan, was made supervisor of the Secretariat, chancellor, and inspector of Yangzhou with full control of state affairs; the Prince of Sui, Liu Dan, was made guard general and inspector of Jingzhou with honors equal to the Three Excellencies; Zang Zhi was made general of the eastern household and inspector of Jiangzhou with the same exalted standing; Shen Qingzhi was made general who leads the army; and Xiao Sihua was made left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以王僧達為右僕射，柳元景為侍中、左衛將軍，宗愨為右衛將軍，張暢為吏部尚書，劉延孫、顏竣並為侍中。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Wang Sengda was made Right Vice Director; Liu Yuanjing was made Palace Attendant and Left Guard General; Zong Que was made Right Guard General; Zhang Chang was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel; and Liu Yansun and Yan Jun were both made Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Wang Sengda was made right vice director; Liu Yuanjing was made palace attendant and left guard general; Zong Que was made right guard general; Zhang Chang was made director of the Ministry of Personnel; and Liu Yansun and Yan Jun were both made palace attendants.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 五月，癸酉朔，臧質以雍州兵二萬至新亭。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day of the guiyou cycle, Zang Zhi arrived at Xinting with twenty thousand Yongzhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day guiyou, Zang Zhi reached Xinting with twenty thousand troops from Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史劉遵考遣其將夏侯獻之帥步騎五千軍於瓜步。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yuzhou, Liu Zunkao, sent his general Xiahou Xianzhi to lead five thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp at Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zunkao, inspector of Yuzhou, sent his general Xiahou Xianzhi with five thousand foot and horse soldiers to encamp at Guabu.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 先是，世祖遣寧朔將軍顧彬之將兵東入，受隨王誕節度。

translations.literal: Previously, Shizu had dispatched General of Resolute Cavalry Gu Binzhi to lead troops eastward, subject to the command of the Prince of Sui, Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Jun had sent General of Resolute Cavalry Gu Binzhi east with an army under the command of Prince Dan of Sui.

sentences.zh: 誕遣參軍劉季之將兵與彬之俱向建康，誕自頓西陵，為之後繼。

translations.literal: Dan sent his aide Liu Jizhi to lead troops together with Binzhi toward Jiankang, while Dan himself encamped at Xiling to follow up in support.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent his aide Liu Jizhi forward with a force to join Binzhi in marching on Jiankang, while he himself held at Xiling to follow with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 劭遣殿中將軍燕欽等拒之，相遇於曲阿奔牛塘，欽等大敗。

translations.literal: Shao dispatched Palace General Yan Qin and others to resist them; they met at Benniu Pond in Qu'e, and Qin and the rest were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Palace General Yan Qin and others to block them; the armies met at Benniu Pond in Qu'e, and Yan Qin was routed.

sentences.zh: 劭於是緣淮樹柵以自守，又決破崗、方山埭以絕東軍。

translations.literal: Shao therefore planted palisades along the Huai to defend himself and also broke the Gang and Fangshan dams to cut off the eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then fortified the Huai line with palisades and breached the Gang and Fangshan dams to sever the eastern army's advance.

sentences.zh: 時男丁既盡，召婦女供役。

translations.literal: By then the adult males were exhausted, and women were summoned to supply labor.
translations.idiomatic: With every able-bodied man already conscripted, he even pressed women into forced labor.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魯秀等募勇士攻大航，克之。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Lu Xiu and others recruited bold warriors to attack the Great Bridge and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Lu Xiu and his allies raised volunteers, stormed the Great Bridge, and took it.

sentences.zh: 王羅漢聞官軍已渡，即放仗降，緣渚幢隊以次奔散，器仗鼓蓋充塞路衢。

translations.literal: Wang Luohan, hearing that the imperial army had crossed, immediately laid down his weapons and surrendered; along the riverbank the banner companies dispersed in succession, and weapons, drums, and parasols choked the roads.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Luohan learned the loyal army had crossed, he surrendered at once; banner units along the shore broke up one after another, and abandoned arms, drums, and parasols littered the streets.

sentences.zh: 是夜，劭閉守六門，於門內鑿塹立柵；

translations.literal: That night, Shao closed and held the six gates, and inside the gates dug ditches and erected palisades;
translations.idiomatic: That night Shao sealed the six city gates and, within them, dug trenches and threw up barricades;

sentences.zh: 城中沸亂，丹陽尹尹弘等文武將吏爭逾城出降。

translations.literal: inside the city there was boiling disorder, and the Prefect of Danyang, Yin Hong, together with civil and military officers and generals, all scrambled over the walls to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: the city erupted in chaos as Danyang prefect Yin Hong and other civil and military officers scrambled over the walls to defect.

sentences.zh: 劭燒輦及兗冕服於宮庭。

translations.literal: Shao burned the imperial carriage and the ceremonial robes and cap at the palace court.
translations.idiomatic: Shao burned the imperial carriage and the full regalia of state in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌宣令所統，皆使解甲，自石頭戴白幡來降；

translations.literal: Xiao Bin proclaimed to those under his command that all were to lay down armor, and he came to surrender from Shitou wearing a white banner;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin ordered his troops to disarm and came from Shitou under a white flag to surrender;

sentences.zh: 詔斬斌於軍門。

translations.literal: an edict ordered Bin executed at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: an edict was issued, and he was beheaded before the army gate.

sentences.zh: 濬勸劭載寶貨逃入海，劭以人情離散，不果行。

translations.literal: Jun urged Shao to load treasure and flee by sea, but Shao, because hearts and loyalties had scattered, did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun urged Shao to load the treasury and escape by sea, but Shao, seeing loyalty collapse all around him, could not bring himself to go.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 乙亥，輔國將軍朱修之克東府，丙子，諸軍克台城，各由諸門入會於殿庭，獲王正見，斬之。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, General Who Supports the State Zhu Xiuzhi captured the Eastern Palace; on the day bingzi, the various armies captured Taicheng, each entered through the various gates and assembled in the hall court, seized Wang Zhengjian, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, General Who Supports the State Zhu Xiuzhi took the Eastern Palace; on bingzi the allied armies stormed Taicheng, poured in through every gate, and gathered in the main hall, where they seized Wang Zhengjian and executed him.

sentences.zh: 張超之走至合殿御床之所。

translations.literal: Zhang Chaozhi fled to the place of the imperial couch in the Hall of Union.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chaozhi fled as far as the imperial bedchamber in the Hall of Union.

sentences.zh: 為軍士所殺，刳腸割心，諸將臠其肉，生啖之。

translations.literal: He was killed by soldiers; they disemboweled him and cut out his heart, and the generals sliced his flesh and ate it raw.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers cut him down, ripped open his belly and tore out his heart, and the generals carved up his flesh and devoured it raw.

sentences.zh: 建平等七王號哭俱出。

translations.literal: Jianping and the other seven princes came out together wailing.
translations.idiomatic: The seven princes, beginning with Jianping, came out together in loud lamentation.

sentences.zh: 劭穿西垣，入武庫井中，隊副高禽執之。

translations.literal: Shao broke through the western wall, entered the armory well, and was seized by the squad deputy Gao Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Shao broke through the western wall, hid in the armory well, and was seized by squad deputy Gao Qin.

sentences.zh: 劭曰：「天子何在？

translations.literal: Shao said, "Where is the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Shao asked, "Where is the emperor?

sentences.zh: 」禽曰：「近在新亭。

translations.literal: " Qin said, "He is recently at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qin answered, "He is at Xinting right now.

sentences.zh: 」至殿前，臧質見之慟哭，劭曰：「天地所不覆載，丈人何為見器？

translations.literal: When they reached the front of the hall, Zang Zhi saw him and wailed; Shao said, "What heaven and earth do not cover and bear—elder, why show such regard?
translations.idiomatic: When they came before the hall, Zang Zhi saw him and wept bitterly; Shao said, "I am one heaven and earth themselves reject—elder, why trouble yourself over me?

sentences.zh: 」又謂質曰：「可得為啟乞遠徙不？

translations.literal: " He also said to Zhi, "Can you petition on my behalf begging banishment to a distant place?
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Zang Zhi, "Will you plead for me to be exiled far away?

sentences.zh: 」質曰：「主上近在航南，自當有處分。

translations.literal: " Zhi said, "The sovereign lord is recently south of the bridge; naturally there will be a disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi replied, "His Majesty is just south of the bridge; he will decide your fate.

sentences.zh: 」縛劭於馬上，防送軍門。

translations.literal: " They bound Shao on horseback and escorted him under guard to the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: They bound Shao to his horse and escorted him under guard to the army gate.

sentences.zh: 時不見傳國璽，以問劭，劭曰：』在嚴道育處。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial seal of transmission was not seen; they questioned Shao, and Shao said, "It is at Yan Daoyu's place.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seal of transmission could not be found; when Shao was questioned, he said, "It is with Yan Daoyu.

sentences.zh: 」就取，得之。

translations.literal: " They went to fetch it and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: They sent men to retrieve it, and the seal was recovered.

sentences.zh: 斬劭及四子於牙下。

translations.literal: Shao and his four sons were beheaded beneath the army standard.
translations.idiomatic: Shao and his four sons were beheaded beneath the army standard.

sentences.zh: 濬帥左右數十人挾南平王鑠南走，遇江夏王義恭於越城。

translations.literal: Jun led several dozen attendants and, taking the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, fled south; they met the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, at Yuecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun fled south with a few dozen followers, dragging the Prince of Nanping, Liu Shuo, with him, and met the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong, at Yuecheng.

sentences.zh: 濬下馬曰：「南中郎今何所作？

translations.literal: Jun dismounted and said, "What is the Southern Central Commander doing now?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun dismounted and asked, "What is the Southern Central Commander up to now?

sentences.zh: 」義恭曰：「上已君臨萬國。

translations.literal: " Yigong said, "The sovereign has already ruled the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong answered, "The Son of Heaven already holds sway over the realm.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「虎頭來得無晚乎？

translations.literal: " He also said, "Has Hutou's coming not been too late?
translations.idiomatic: Jun pressed him, "So Tiger Head's arrival was not too late after all?

sentences.zh: 」義恭曰：「殊當恨晚。

translations.literal: " Yigong said, "Especially ought one to regret that it was late.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong said, "All the more reason to regret how late it was.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「故當不死邪？

translations.literal: " He also said, "So should one not die after all?
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked again, "Then am I not to die?

sentences.zh: 」義恭曰：「可詣行闕請罪。

translations.literal: " Yigong said, "One may go to the traveling palace gate to plead guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong said, "You may go to the traveling palace and plead guilty.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「未審猶疑賜一職自效不？

translations.literal: " He also said, "I do not yet know—might one still be granted one office to repay with service?
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked, "Do you think there is still a chance I may be given some post and allowed to serve?

sentences.zh: 」義恭又曰：「此未可量。

translations.literal: " Yigong again said, "That cannot yet be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong answered again, "That I cannot say.

sentences.zh: 」勒與俱歸，於道斬之，及其三子。

translations.literal: " He compelled Jun to return with him, and on the road executed him and his three sons.
translations.idiomatic: He forced Liu Jun to turn back with him, and on the road had him and his three sons executed.

sentences.zh: 劭、濬父子首並梟於大航，暴屍於市。

translations.literal: The heads of Shao and Jun, father and son, were together displayed at the Great Bridge, and their corpses were exposed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: The heads of Shao and Liu Jun, father and son, were hung at the Great Bridge, and their bodies were left to rot in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 劭妃殷氏及劭、濬諸女、妾媵，皆賜死於獄。

translations.literal: Shao's consort, Lady Yin, together with Shao's and Jun's daughters and concubines, were all granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's consort, Lady Yin, together with the daughters and concubines of Shao and Liu Jun, were all ordered to take their own lives in prison.

sentences.zh: 污瀦劭所居齋。

translations.literal: Shao's residence chamber was turned into a cesspool.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's private quarters were defiled and flooded into a cesspool.

sentences.zh: 殷氏且死，謂獄丞江恪曰：「汝家骨肉相殘，何以枉殺無罪人？

translations.literal: As Lady Yin was about to die, she said to the prison warden Jiang Ke, "Your house has kin slaying kin—why wrongly kill one without crime?
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Lady Yin said to prison warden Jiang Ke, "Your own house butchered its own blood—why kill an innocent woman?

sentences.zh: 」恪曰：』受拜皇后，非罪而何？

translations.literal: " Ke said, "Having received appointment as empress—if not crime, then what?
translations.idiomatic: Ke replied, "You accepted the title of empress—if that is not guilt, what is?

sentences.zh: 」殷氏曰：「此權時耳，當以鸚鵡為後。

translations.literal: " Lady Yin said, "That was only expedient for the moment; one ought to have made Yingwu empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin said, "That was only a stopgap; the throne should have gone to Yingwu.

sentences.zh: 」褚湛之之南奔也，濬即與褚妃離絕，故免於誅。

translations.literal: " When Chu Zhanzhi fled south, Jun immediately severed ties with Chu's consort, and therefore escaped execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Zhanzhi fled south, Liu Jun at once cast off Chu's daughter as his wife, which spared her from execution.

sentences.zh: 嚴道育、王鸚鵡並都街鞭殺，焚屍，揚灰於江。

translations.literal: Yan Daoyu and Wang Yingwu were both flogged to death in the public street; their corpses were burned and the ashes scattered on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Daoyu and Wang Yingwu were both flogged to death in the street; their bodies were burned and the ashes cast into the river.

sentences.zh: 殷沖、尹弘、王羅漢及淮南太守沈璞皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Yin Chong, Yin Hong, Wang Luohan, and the Administrator of Huainan, Shen Pu, all suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chong, Yin Hong, Wang Luohan, and Huainan administrator Shen Pu were all put to death.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 庚辰，解嚴，辛巳，帝如東府，百官請罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, the martial law was lifted; on the day xinsi, the emperor went to the Eastern Palace, and the hundred officials pleaded guilt; an edict released them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the martial law was lifted; on xinsi the emperor visited the Eastern Palace, where officials begged forgiveness, and an edict pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 甲申，尊帝母路淑媛為皇太后。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, the emperor's mother, Lady Lu the Pure and Honored, was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the emperor's mother, Lady Lu the Pure and Honored, was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was a native of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was a native of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，立妃王氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, the consort, Lady Wang, was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the consort Lady Wang was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 後父偃，導之玄孫也。

translations.literal: The empress's father Yan was the great-great-grandson of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wang Yan was the great-great-grandson of Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以柳元景為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, Liu Yuanjing was made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Liu Yuanjing was appointed inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，追贈袁淑為太尉，謚忠憲公；

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Yuan Shu was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant with the posthumous title Loyal and Lawful Duke;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Yuan Shu was posthumously enfeoffed as grand commandant with the title Loyal and Lawful Duke;

sentences.zh: 徐湛之為司空，謚忠烈公；

translations.literal: Xu Zhanzhi was made Minister of Works with the posthumous title Loyal and Fiery Duke;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhanzhi was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of works with the title Loyal and Fiery Duke;

sentences.zh: 江湛為開府儀同三司，謚忠簡公；

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan was made Grand Prefect of an Establishment with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongjian (Loyal and Simple).
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan received the rank of grand prefect with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and was posthumously created Duke of Zhongjian, the Loyal and Simple.

sentences.zh: 王僧綽為金紫光祿大夫，謚簡侯。

translations.literal: Wang Sengchuo was made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle and was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Jian (Simple).
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengchuo was raised to grand master of the golden seal and purple girdle and posthumously ennobled as Marquis of Jian, the Simple.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以太尉義恭為揚、南徐二州刺史，進位太傅，領大司馬。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Grand Commandant Yigong was made Inspector of Yangzhou and South Xuzhou, promoted to Grand Tutor, and additionally appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Grand Commandant Liu Yigong was given Yangzhou and South Xuzhou, elevated to grand tutor, and made grand marshal as well.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 初，劭以尚書令何尚之為司空、領尚書令，子征北長史偃為侍中，父子並居權要。

translations.literal: Initially, Shao had made He Shangzhi, Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Minister of Works while retaining the Ministry of the Secretariat; his son Yan, chief secretary on the Northern Campaign staff, was made Palace Attendant; father and son both held positions of decisive power.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shao had kept He Shangzhi as minister of the secretariat while also making him grand minister of works, and had appointed Shangzhi's son Yan, chief secretary on the northern expedition staff, palace attendant—father and son alike at the heart of power.

sentences.zh: 及劭敗，尚之左右皆散，自洗黃閣。

translations.literal: When Shao was defeated, Shangzhi's attendants all scattered, and he himself cleaned the Yellow Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After Shao's fall Shangzhi's staff melted away, and he scrubbed the Yellow Pavilion with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 殷沖等既誅，人為之寒心。

translations.literal: After Yin Chong and the others had been executed, people were chilled at heart on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yin Chong and his associates were put to death, everyone feared for Shangzhi's life.

sentences.zh: 帝以尚之、偃素有令譽，且居劭朝用智將迎，時有全脫，故特免之，復以尚之為尚書令，偃為大司馬長史，任遇無改。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Shangzhi and Yan had long enjoyed a fine reputation and, during Shao's reign, had used their wits to receive and protect him and at times had secured his full escape, specially pardoned them, restored Shangzhi as Minister of the Secretariat and Yan as chief secretary to the Grand Marshal, and left their appointments and favor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared them because Shangzhi and Yan were men of established repute who, even under Shao, had more than once used their wit to shield him and see him safely through; Shangzhi was restored to the secretariat and Yan to the grand marshal's staff, with rank and favor undiminished.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 甲午，帝謁初寧、長寧陵。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, the emperor visited the tombs at Chuning and Changning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the emperor paid his respects at the Chuning and Changning tombs.

sentences.zh: 追贈卜天與益州刺史，謚壯侯，與袁叔等四家，長給稟祿。

translations.literal: Bu Tianyu was posthumously granted the post of Inspector of Yizhou and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuang; he, together with Yuan Shu and three other households, was granted stipend grain in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Tianyu was posthumously made inspector of Yizhou and created Marquis of Zhuang; his house, with Yuan Shu's and three others, received grain stipends for all time.

sentences.zh: 張泓之等各贈郡守。

translations.literal: Zhang Hongzhi and the others were each posthumously granted the rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongzhi and his fellows were each posthumously given prefectural rank.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以南平王鑠為司空，建平王宏為尚書左僕射，蕭思話為中書令、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Prince Shuo of Nanping was made Grand Minister of Works; Prince Hong of Jianping was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Xiao Sihua was made Director of the Central Secretariat and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Prince Shuo of Nanping became grand minister of works; Prince Hong of Jianping became left vice director of the secretariat; and Xiao Sihua was made director of the central secretariat and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙午，帝還宮。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day bingwu, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingwu, the emperor went back to the palace.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 初，帝之討西陽蠻也，臧質使柳元景將兵會之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was campaigning against the Xiyang barbarians, Zang Zhi had sent Liu Yuanjing with troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had marched against the Xiyang tribes, Zang Zhi had dispatched Liu Yuanjing with an army to link up with him.

sentences.zh: 及質起兵，欲奉南譙王義宣為主，潛使元景帥所領西還，元景即以質書呈帝，語其信曰：「臧冠軍當是未知殿下義舉耳。

translations.literal: When Zhi raised troops, wishing to install Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao as leader, he secretly ordered Yuanjing to lead his command westward; Yuanjing thereupon presented Zhi's letter to the emperor and told the messenger: "General Zang probably does not yet know of Your Highness's righteous undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi rebelled and sought to make Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao his figurehead, he secretly told Yuanjing to march west with his troops; Yuanjing instead handed Zhi's letter to the emperor and said to the courier: "General Zang must not yet have heard of Your Highness's loyal rising.

sentences.zh: 方應伐逆，不容西還。

translations.literal: We ought just now to campaign against the rebel; withdrawal to the west cannot be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: We are about to strike the usurper; a return west is out of the question.

sentences.zh: 」質以此恨之。

translations.literal: " Zhi resented him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi never forgave him for it.

sentences.zh: 及元景為雍州，質慮其為荊、江後患，建議元景當為爪牙，不宜遠出。

translations.literal: When Yuanjing became Inspector of Yongzhou, Zhi feared he would become a later trouble for Jing and Jiang and recommended that Yuanjing should serve as his claw and fang and ought not be sent far away.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuanjing was made inspector of Yongzhou, Zhi worried he would one day threaten Jing and Jiang and urged that Yuanjing be kept at his side as enforcer rather than posted far off.

sentences.zh: 帝重違其言，戊申，以元景為護軍將軍，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: The emperor was loath to go against his words; on the day wushen, Yuanjing was made General Who Guards the Army and put in charge of the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to defy Zhi outright, the emperor on wushen made Yuanjing general who guards the army and commander of the Shitou fortress.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 己酉，以司州刺史魯爽為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, Lu Shuang, Inspector of Si, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Lu Shuang, inspector of Si, was transferred to South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以衛軍司馬徐遺寶為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Xu Yibao, chief secretary of the Guard Army, was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Xu Yibao, chief secretary on the guard army staff, was appointed inspector of Yanzhou.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔有司論功行賞，封顏竣等為公、侯。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, an edict ordered the relevant offices to assess merit and grant rewards; Yan Jun and others were enfeoffed as dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the throne commanded a review of service and distribution of rewards; Yan Jun and others were created dukes and marquises.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 辛未，徙南譙王義宣為南郡王，隨王誕為竟陵王，立義宣次子宜陽侯愷為南譙王。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao was transferred to become Prince of Nanjun; Prince Dan of Sui was made Prince of Jingling; and Yixuan's second son, Marquis Kai of Yiyang, was established as Prince of Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao was redesignated prince of Nanjun; Prince Dan of Sui became prince of Jingling; and Yixuan's second son, Marquis Kai of Yiyang, was invested as the new Prince of Nanqiao.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬申，以領軍將軍沈慶之為南兗州刺史，鎮盱眙。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day renshen, Shen Qingzhi, General Who Leads the Army, was made Inspector of South Yanzhou and garrisoned at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on renshen, Shen Qingzhi, general who leads the army, was sent to South Yanzhou and stationed at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以柳元景為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, Liu Yuanjing was made General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Liu Yuanjing was appointed general who leads the army.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏太皇太后赫連氏殂。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, the Wei Empress Dowager Helian died.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Wei empress dowager, Lady Helian, passed away.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 丞相義宣固辭內任及子愷王爵。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yixuan firmly declined an interior appointment and the princely rank for his son Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Liu Yixuan repeatedly refused a capital post and the princely title for his son Kai.

sentences.zh: 甲午，更以義宣為荊、湘二州刺史，愷為宜陽縣王，將佐以下並加賞秩。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Yixuan was again made Inspector of Jingzhou and Xiangzhou; Kai was made Prince of Yiyang county; and officers and aides from the rank of general downward were all granted additional rewards and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Yixuan was again given Jing and Xiang; Kai was made prince of Yiyang county; and every officer and aide from general down received extra honors.

sentences.zh: 以竟陵王誕為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince Dan of Jingling was made Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Jingling was appointed inspector of Yangzhou.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day xinchou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the first day xinchou, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔求直言。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, an edict sought forthright criticism.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the throne called for blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔省細作並尚方雕文塗飾；

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, an edict reduced fine crafts and the carved, painted, and decorated work of the imperial workshops.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou an edict cut back luxury crafts and ornamental work in the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 貴戚競利，悉皆禁絕。

translations.literal: Imperial kinsmen competing for profit were all forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Every form of profit-seeking among the imperial clan was banned outright.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 中軍錄事參軍周朗上疏，以為：「毒之在體，必割其緩處。

translations.literal: Zhou Lang, recording secretary on the Central Army staff, submitted a memorial, saying: "When poison is in the body, one must cut away the swollen part.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lang, recording secretary on the central army staff, memorialized the throne: "Poison in the flesh must be cut out where it festers.

sentences.zh: 歷下、泗間，不足戍守。

translations.literal: The region of Lixia and the Si River cannot adequately be garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Lixia and the country around the Si cannot be held with the forces we have.

sentences.zh: 議者必以為胡衰不足避，而不知我之病甚於胡矣。

translations.literal: Counselors will surely say the barbarians are in decline and need not be avoided, yet they do not know that our illness is worse than the barbarians'.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers will tell you the Hu are fading and can be ignored—but our own sickness runs deeper than theirs.

sentences.zh: 今空守孤城，徒費財役。

translations.literal: Now we hold empty isolated cities in vain, merely wasting wealth and labor.
translations.idiomatic: We squat in empty outposts and bleed treasure and manpower for nothing.

sentences.zh: 使虜但發輕騎三千，更互出入，春來犯麥，秋至侵禾，水陸漕輸，居然復絕；

translations.literal: If the enemy need only send three thousand light cavalry to raid in rotation, coming in spring to trample the wheat and in autumn to ravage the grain, then waterborne and overland transport will altogether cease again.
translations.idiomatic: Let the foe send three thousand light horse to raid in turn—trampling the wheat in spring, cutting the harvest in autumn—and river and road supply will fail altogether.

sentences.zh: 於賊不勞而邊已困，不至二年，卒散民盡，可蹺足而待也。

translations.literal: The enemy will exert no effort while the frontier is already exhausted; within two years the soldiers will scatter and the people be spent—one may wait for that with folded legs.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy need not lift a finger while the border collapses; in less than two years the armies will dissolve and the people be gone—and that end can be watched for with arms folded.

sentences.zh: 今人知不以羊追狼、蟹捕鼠，而令重車弱卒與肥與悍胡相逐，其不能濟固宜矣。

translations.literal: People today know not to set sheep on wolves or crabs on rats, yet we make heavy chariots and weak soldiers pursue fat, fierce Hu— that they cannot succeed is only to be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows you do not hunt wolves with sheep or mice with crabs, yet we send lumbering wagons and weary foot soldiers to chase down plump, savage Hu—small wonder they fail.

sentences.zh: 又，三年之喪，天下之達喪；

translations.literal: Again, the three years of mourning is the universal mourning of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Again: three years' mourning is the mourning ordained for all the world.

sentences.zh: 漢氏節其臣則可矣，薄其子則亂也。

translations.literal: For the Han to shorten it for their ministers was acceptable; to stint their sons is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han curtailed it for officials, that was tolerable; to pare it for a son is to invite chaos.

sentences.zh: 凡法有變於古而刻於情，則莫能順焉；

translations.literal: Whenever a law departs from antiquity and is harsh toward natural feeling, none can follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Any rule that breaks with the old ways and cuts against the heart will find no willing obedience.

sentences.zh: 至乎敗於禮而安於身，必遽而奉之。

translations.literal: As for those who fail in ritual yet find comfort for themselves, they rush to adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Men who betray propriety yet soothe their own conscience will seize on such changes at once.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以大孝始基，宜反斯謬。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has founded your rule upon great filial piety; you ought to reverse this error.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has taken the throne under the banner of supreme filial duty—this mistake should be undone.

sentences.zh: 又，舉天下以奉一君，何患不給？

translations.literal: Again, if the whole realm supports one sovereign, what worry is there of insufficiency?
translations.idiomatic: Again: if the empire feeds one ruler, how could want remain?

sentences.zh: 一體炫金，不及百兩，一歲美衣，不過數襲；

translations.literal: Gold adornment for one body amounts to less than a hundred taels; fine clothes for one year come to no more than a few suits.
translations.idiomatic: Ornaments of gold on a single person need not reach a hundred taels; splendid dress for a year need not exceed a few changes.

sentences.zh: 而必收寶連櫝，集服累笥，目豈常視，身未時親，是櫝帶寶、笥著衣也，何糜蠹之劇，惑鄙之甚邪！

translations.literal: Yet one must gather treasures in linked boxes and pile garments in stacked chests—eyes cannot often see them, the body cannot often wear them; this is wearing the box with the jewels and wearing the chest with the clothes—what extravagance of waste, what depth of folly!
translations.idiomatic: Yet treasures are hoarded box upon box and robes chest upon chest—seldom seen, seldom worn: jewels carried in their cases, clothes borne in their trunks. What ruinous waste, what vulgar delusion!

sentences.zh: 且細作始並，以為儉節；

translations.literal: Moreover, fine crafts were at first combined in order to promote thrift.
translations.idiomatic: Fine workshops were first consolidated to enforce frugality.

sentences.zh: 而市造華怪，即傳於民。

translations.literal: Yet when the market workshops produce lavish and strange things, they are immediately passed on to the people.
translations.idiomatic: But when the market ateliers turn out gaudy novelties, those fashions spill straight into the streets.

sentences.zh: 如此，則遷也，非罷也。

translations.literal: In this way it is relocation, not abolition.
translations.idiomatic: That is relocation, not repeal.

sentences.zh: 凡闕庶民，制度日侈，見車馬不辯貴賤，視冠服不知尊卑。

translations.literal: Among the common folk everywhere, institutions grow daily more extravagant; seeing chariots and horses, one cannot distinguish noble from base; seeing caps and robes, one cannot tell high from low.
translations.idiomatic: Among ordinary people custom grows more lavish by the day—carriages and horses no longer mark rank, caps and robes no longer signal status.

sentences.zh: 尚方今造一物，小民明已睥睨；

translations.literal: When the imperial workshop today makes one thing, commoners tomorrow already covet it.
translations.idiomatic: What the imperial workshop fashions today, commoners are already eyeing tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 宮中朝制一衣，庶家晚已裁學。

translations.literal: When the palace sets one morning garment, common households by evening are already cutting and imitating it.
translations.idiomatic: A robe cut for the morning court is copied in common homes before nightfall.

sentences.zh: 侈麗之源，實先宮閫。

translations.literal: The source of lavishness truly begins in the inner quarters of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The fount of excess is the palace itself.

sentences.zh: 又，設官者宜官稱事立，人稱官置。

translations.literal: Again, in establishing offices, offices should be titled to match affairs and men appointed to match offices.
translations.idiomatic: Again: offices should be named for the work they do, and men chosen for the offices they can fill.

sentences.zh: 王侯識未堪務，不應強仕。

translations.literal: Princes and marquises whose understanding cannot yet bear affairs ought not be forced into office.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and marquises whose minds are not yet equal to duty should not be pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 且帝子未官，人誰謂賤？

translations.literal: Moreover, if an imperial son holds no office, who will call him base?
translations.idiomatic: A prince without a post is still a prince—who would deem him low?

sentences.zh: 但宜詳置賓友，茂擇正人，亦何必列長史、參軍、別架從事，然後為貴哉！

translations.literal: One need only carefully appoint companions and richly choose upright men—why must one array chief secretaries, military aides, and administrative staff before one is accounted noble?
translations.idiomatic: Choose worthy companions and upright mentors—that is enough; why must a prince stack his household with chief secretaries, aides, and staff before he counts as grand?

sentences.zh: 又，俗好以毀沈人，不知察其所以致毀；

translations.literal: Again, custom likes to advance men through slander and ruin, without examining why they were slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Again: the age loves to ruin men by rumor without asking why they were ruined.

sentences.zh: 以譽進人，不知測其所以致譽。

translations.literal: It likes to promote men through praise, without measuring why they were praised.
translations.idiomatic: It loves to elevate men by praise without testing why they were praised.

sentences.zh: 毀徒皆鄙，則宜擢其毀者；

translations.literal: If those who slander are all base, then one ought to promote those who slander.
translations.idiomatic: If every accuser is a scoundrel, promote the accusers.

sentences.zh: 譽黨悉庸，則宜退其譽者。

translations.literal: If the parties of praise are all mediocre, then one ought to demote those who praise.
translations.idiomatic: If every flatterer's circle is dull, demote the flatterers.

sentences.zh: 如此，則毀譽不妄，善惡分矣。

translations.literal: In this way slander and praise will not be random, and good and evil will be divided.
translations.idiomatic: Then blame and praise will not lie, and merit and fault will stand apart.

sentences.zh: 凡無世不有言事，無時不有下令。

translations.literal: Generally, no age lacks memorials, and no time lacks edicts.
translations.idiomatic: No reign lacks remonstrance; no year lacks decrees.

sentences.zh: 然昇平不至，昏危相繼，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet peace never arrives, and confusion and danger follow in succession—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet tranquillity never comes, and turmoil follows turmoil—why?

sentences.zh: 設令之本非實故也。

translations.literal: Because the foundations of institutions and edicts are not genuine.
translations.idiomatic: Because the roots of policy and command are hollow.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，忤旨，自解去職。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; it offended the emperor, and Lang resigned his office of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne, crossed the emperor, and Zhou Lang resigned on his own.

sentences.zh: 朗，嶠之弟也。

translations.literal: Lang was the younger brother of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lang was a younger brother of Zhou Jiao.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 侍中謝莊上言：「詔云：『貴戚競利，悉皆禁絕。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Xie Zhuang submitted a statement: "The edict says: 'Imperial kinsmen competing for profit are all forbidden.'
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xie Zhuang wrote: "The edict reads: 'Imperial kinsmen who scramble for profit are forbidden altogether.'"

sentences.zh: 』此實允愜民聽。

translations.literal: This truly accords with what the people wish to hear.
translations.idiomatic: That truly satisfies what the people long to hear.

sentences.zh: 若有犯違，則應依制裁糾；

translations.literal: If there are violations, they ought to be punished and corrected according to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone breaks it, the law should strike.

sentences.zh: 若廢法申恩，便為明詔既下而聲實乘爽也。

translations.literal: If the law is set aside to show favor, then after a clear edict has been issued, word and reality will diverge.
translations.idiomatic: If the law is waived for favor, a bright decree will mean nothing the moment it is broken.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂大臣在祿位者，尤不宜與民爭利。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly thinks that great ministers who hold salaried posts especially ought not compete with the people for profit.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly submit that great ministers on the public payroll above all must not haggle with common folk for gain.

sentences.zh: 不審可得在此詔不？

translations.literal: May I ask whether this edict applies to them as well?
translations.idiomatic: Are they included under this edict?

sentences.zh: 」莊，弘微之子也。

translations.literal: " Zhuang was the son of Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhuang was a son of Xie Hongwei.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 上多變易太祖之制，郡縣以三周為滿，宋之善政，於是乎衰。

translations.literal: The emperor frequently altered the institutions of Emperor Taizu; prefectures and counties took three cycles as a full term—and the good governance of Song declined from this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept overturning Taizu's rules, shortening prefectural and county terms to three review cycles—and with that, Song's best practices withered.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏濮陽王閭若文、征西大將軍永昌王仁皆坐謀叛，仁賜死於長安，若文伏誅。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, the Wei Prince Ruowen of Puyang and the General Who Conquers the West, Prince Ren of Yongchang, were both charged with plotting rebellion; Ren was granted death at Chang'an, and Ruowen was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the Wei Prince Ruowen of Puyang and Prince Ren of Yongchang, general who conquers the west, were both convicted of treason; Ren was allowed to die at Chang'an and Ruowen was beheaded.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 南平穆王鑠素負才能，意當輕上；

translations.literal: Prince Shuo of Nanping, posthumously Mu, had always possessed talent and was presumed to look down upon the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuo of Nanping, later styled Mu, was a man of real ability and was thought to hold the emperor in contempt.

sentences.zh: 又為太子劭所任，出降最晚。

translations.literal: He had also been trusted by Crown Prince Shao and was the last to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had relied on him, and among the defectors he came in last.

sentences.zh: 上潛使人毒之，己巳，鑠卒，贈司徒，以商臣之謚謚之。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly sent men to poison him; on the day jisi Shuo died; he was posthumously granted the post of Minister Over the Masses and given the posthumous title Shangchen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him poisoned in secret; on jisi Shuo died, was posthumously made minister over the masses, and was given the posthumous name Shangchen—the same borne by the parricide of Chu.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 南海太守蕭簡據廣州反。

translations.literal: Xiao Jian, Administrator of Nanhai, seized Guangzhou and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jian, prefect of Nanhai, seized Guangzhou and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 簡，斌之弟也。

translations.literal: Jian was the younger brother of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jian was a younger brother of Xiao Bin.

sentences.zh: 詔新南海太守南昌鄧琬、始興太守沈法系討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the new Administrator of Nanhai, Deng Wan of Nanchang, and the Administrator of Shixing, Shen Faxue, to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the new Nanhai prefect Deng Wan of Nanchang and Shixing prefect Shen Faxue to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 法系，慶之之從弟也。

translations.literal: Faxue was the younger cousin of Qingzhi on his father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Faxue was a paternal cousin of Shen Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 簡誑其眾曰：「台軍是賊劭所遣。

translations.literal: Jian deceived his masses, saying, "The Terrace army was sent by the traitor Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jian lied to his troops, saying, "The imperial army was sent by the traitor Shao.

sentences.zh: 」眾信之，為之固守。

translations.literal: " The masses believed him and held firm on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The men believed him and fought on stubbornly for him.

sentences.zh: 琬先至，止為一攻道；

translations.literal: Wan arrived first and made only one assault route;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan arrived first and opened only a single line of attack;

sentences.zh: 法系至，曰：「宜四面並攻；

translations.literal: when Faxue arrived, he said, "One ought to attack on all four sides together;
translations.idiomatic: when Shen Faxue came up, he said, "We should assault from all four sides at once;

sentences.zh: 若守一道，何時可拔！

translations.literal: if we hold to one route, when can it be taken!
translations.idiomatic: if we stick to one avenue, when will the place ever fall!

sentences.zh: 」琬不從。

translations.literal: " Wan would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan refused.

sentences.zh: 法系曰：「更相申五十日。

translations.literal: Faxue said, "Let us extend the term by fifty days more."
translations.idiomatic: Faxue said, "Give me fifty more days."

sentences.zh: 」日盡又不克，乃從之。

translations.literal: " When the days were exhausted and he still could not overcome, Wan then followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the fifty days passed and the city still held, Wan at last agreed.

sentences.zh: 八道俱攻，一日即破之。

translations.literal: Eight routes attacked together, and in one day they broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Eight assault columns struck together and took the city in a single day.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁卯，斬簡，廣州平。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingmao, Jian was beheaded and Guangzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingmao, Xiao Jian was executed and Guangzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 法系封府庫付琬而還。

translations.literal: Faxue sealed the government treasury, handed it over to Wan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Faxue sealed the government stores, turned them over to Wan, and marched back.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，丙午，以左軍將軍魯秀為司州刺史。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on bingwu, Left Army General Lu Xiu was made Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on bingwu, Lu Xiu, Left Army General, was appointed inspector of Si Province.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏主如信都、中山。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Wei ruler went to Xindu and Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Wei emperor traveled to Xindu and Zhongshan.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸未，以將置東宮，省太子率更令等官，中庶子等各減舊員之半。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on guiwei, because the Eastern Palace was about to be established, the offices of the crown prince's Director of Reckoning and others were reduced, and the palace aides and the rest were each cut to half their former complement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guiwei, with the Eastern Palace about to be installed, the crown prince's director of reckoning and related offices were abolished, and the palace aides and others were each reduced to half their former numbers.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)

sentences.zh: 甲午，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

translations.literal: (End of entry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Paragraph break.)
